description: Port Alexandria cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. The port's schedule lists all ships (in links) with cruises going to or leaving from Alexandria, Egypt, Cairo. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link. Alexandria (port locode EGALY) is Egypt's second-largest city (after the capital Cairo ) and principal cargo port on the Mediterranean Sea (Northern Africa). The city extends 32 km (20 mi) along the coast and has population around 5,2 million. Port Alexandria serves over 80% of the country's trade (imports and exports). The city is also a major industrial center with heavy industries benefitting from natural gas and oil pipelines out of Suez City. Alexandria is one of the cruise ports to Cairo, together with Sokhna and Port Said . The Port of Alexandria has 4 ports - Western Port (Egypt's main seaport that handles ~60% of all imports/exports), Dekhela Port (west of Western Port), Eastern Port (marina/yacht harbor) and Abu Qir Port (handling bulk cargoes, including phosphates and general cargo). Scheduled for inauguration in 2022, Port Alexandia's new containership terminal (Pier 55) will be operated by CMA-CGM - the world's 3rd- largest container shipping company . The concession deal includes CMA-CGM to develop modern logistics, implement digital solutions and training programs, port infrastructure investments. The Pier 55 Terminal covers ~0,56 km2 (0,22 mi2) with total quay length 2+ km and annual capacity ~1,5 million TEU-containers. The city has two international airports - Borg El Arab (approx 25 km / 16 mi from downtown) and El Nouzha , but currently, only Borg El Arab Airport is operational. Borg El Arab Airport serves regularly scheduled flights connecting to Jordan, Qatar ( Doha ), Saudi Arabia, Kuwait City , UAE ( Dubai , Abu Dhabi , Sharjah ), Oman ( Muscat ), Libya, Turkey ( Istanbul ), Italy (Bergamo, Milano). Seasonal flights connect to Greece ( Athens ). Four highways connect Alexandria with Cairo and Mersa Matruh (along the coast). Cairo City is approx 220 km (137 mi) to the southeast (~2,5 hours drive). Alexandria Metro (USD 1,5 billion underground traffic project) was planned to start in 2020 and be completed in 2022. Alexandria was established by Alexander the Great and became a major center for almost 1000 years as the capital of Egypt during the times of Hellenistic, Roman and Byzantine Egypt. Following Egypt's Muslim conquest (in 641 AD) the capital was moved to Fustat (later merged with Cairo). The Pharos (Lighthouse of Alexandria) was one of the Ancient World's Seven Wonders, while the Necropolis was one of the Middle Ages' Seven Wonders. The Great Library of Alexandria (accidentally burned by Julius Caesar) was one of the world's tallest buildings and had the largest collection of manuscripts. At its peak, Alexandria was the world's second most powerful city - after Rome . The city's international shipping trade started to develop in the late-18th century when Egypt became a major exporter of cotton and profited from the overland connection between the Mediterranean and Red Sea (Asia). Independent with some planning or transport. Alexandria’s main sights are spread across a large, busy city. Central streets and the Corniche can be explored independently, but taxis or a pre-arranged car are useful for reaching the archaeological sites efficiently. A guided tour is preferable for visitors who want historical interpretation or several major sights in one day. Cairo and the Giza pyramids require a very long excursion, with roughly 3–3.5 hours of driving each way. Choose this only during a sufficiently long port call, preferably through the cruise line or a reputable operator offering port pickup and a firm return plan.
getting_from_port: Cruise ships normally dock at the passenger terminal inside Alexandria’s large Western Harbour rather than tendering. From the ship, passengers pass through the terminal area and continue to the port gate. Depending on the berth, reaching the gate may itself involve a walk of around 10–15 minutes. Walking: The edge of central Alexandria is approximately 1.5–2 km (0.9–1.2 mi) from the cruise terminal, but the exact distance depends on the berth and passenger exit. The surroundings are busy and walking conditions can be uneven. Taxis: Usually the most practical independent option. Confirm the destination and fare before departure if the vehicle is not metered. Keep small Egyptian-pound notes where possible. Ship transport: Some cruise lines may provide a shuttle or excursion transfer, but this varies by sailing and should be checked onboard. Public transport: Alexandria has trams and local buses, but crowded vehicles, limited visitor information and slow journeys make them less useful during a short port call.
terminal_notes: Scheduled for inauguration in 2022, Port Alexandia's new containership terminal (Pier 55) will be operated by CMA-CGM - the world's 3rd- largest container shipping company . The Pier 55 Terminal covers ~0,56 km2 (0,22 mi2) with total quay length 2+ km and annual capacity ~1,5 million TEU-containers.

things_to_do.name: Alexandria Highlights by Car
things_to_do.description: Allow approximately 5–7 hours for a practical circuit covering the Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa, Pompey’s Pillar, the Roman remains at Kom el-Dikka, the Bibliotheca Alexandrina and the Citadel of Qaitbay. These places are distributed across the city, so a taxi, private car or guided tour saves considerable time. The catacombs include underground chambers and stairs and may not suit visitors with limited mobility. A guide is valuable because relatively little survives above ground from ancient Alexandria.

things_to_do.name: Citadel, Waterfront and Historic Districts
things_to_do.description: For a less rushed day, take a taxi to the Citadel of Qaitbay and explore the western end of the Corniche. The citadel occupies the site traditionally associated with the ancient Pharos lighthouse. Nearby stops can include the fishing harbour, Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque exterior and the streets around Anfushi. Allow 3–4 hours, including transport and time inside the citadel. This option is manageable independently, although traffic and wide road crossings require care.

things_to_do.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina and the Eastern Corniche
things_to_do.description: The modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina contains a monumental reading room, museums and exhibition spaces, although access to individual areas can vary. Combine it with a walk along the seafront and, if time permits, the nearby archaeological remains at Kom el-Dikka. Allow approximately 3–4 hours. A taxi from the port is recommended, followed by walking between nearby sights. Confirm the library’s visitor access and opening arrangements for the day of the call.

things_to_do.name: Cairo and the Giza Pyramids
things_to_do.description: This is an excursion rather than a local sightseeing option. The road journey normally takes about 3–3.5 hours each way and can be longer in traffic. A typical visit consumes 11–13 hours and leaves limited time at the attractions. Organized excursion recommended. The trip is realistic only when the ship has a long stay in Alexandria. The cruise line’s excursion offers the greatest protection if traffic delays the return. Independent rail or bus travel is unsuitable for most same-day cruise visitors because of transfers, variable journey times and the distance between Cairo stations and Giza.

things_to_do.name: Qaitbay Citadel to the Bibliotheca Alexandrina
things_to_do.description: This seafront route is suitable for passengers who enjoy a substantial urban walk and do not need to cover the inland archaeological sites. Take a taxi from the port to the Citadel of Qaitbay. Visit the citadel and view the Eastern Harbour. Walk past the fishing harbour toward Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque. Continue along the Corniche beside the Eastern Harbour. Pass the waterfront around Saad Zaghloul Square and central Alexandria. Finish at the Bibliotheca Alexandrina. Distance: approximately 5 km (3.1 mi). Pure walking time: about 1–1.5 hours. Recommended total: 4–5 hours with the citadel, waterfront stops and library. Difficulty: moderate, mainly flat but exposed to sun, traffic, noise and frequent road crossings. Return to the ship by taxi rather than retracing the route. Allow extra time to negotiate traffic and to walk from the port gate back through the terminal area.
things_to_do.difficulty: moderate, mainly flat but exposed to sun, traffic, noise and frequent road crossings

The port's schedule lists all ships (in links) with cruises going to or leaving from Algeciras, Spain. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link. Algeciras (порт лоцоде ESALG) is a major ferry port and city in Spain's Cadiz Province in Andalusia (autonomous region) with population around 120,000 (metro around 270,000). Algeciras is just approx 20 km (12 mi) northeast of Tarifa (on Costa de la Luz), ranked as one of the world's best windsports destinations. The road distance between Algeciras and Cadiz is ~110 km (68 mi) via A381 Highway. The road distance to Gibraltar UK is ~30 km (19 mi) via A7 Highway. Puerto Algeciras is ranked one of Europe's largest ports by the number of annually handled container ships , cargoes and transhipments. The port's businesses serve commercial shipping (TEU-containers, various cargoes), commercial fishing, passenger shipping (mainly via ferries , also cruise shipping), bunker fueling. Algeciras benefits from its strategic location (near Gibraltar Strait) and, by annual transshipment volume,s is amongst the world's busiest. Port facilities are located in Algeciras as well as in other towns part of the metro region (including San Roque, Los Barrios, Tarifa). In FY2015, by cargo shipping volumes (~100 million tons), Port Algeciras was ranked Spain's and the Mediterranean's largest. By container shipping volumes (2.8 million TEUs in 2010), the port is ranked the world's 31st-largest. Daily scheduled ferry connections link Algeciras with Ceuta (Spanish Morocco) and Tangier Med ( Morocco). These routes are operated by the companies BALEARIA , TRASMEDITERRANEA , FRS (Forde Reederei Seetouristik/Fast Reliable Seaways). Algeciras is also an industrial city, has a well-developed fishing industry, and from here are exported various regionally-farmed agricultural products (cereals, tobacco) and livestock. The tourism industry is also growing, with popular day tours from Algeciras to Tarifa and Gibraltar, and also scenic boat cruises in the Bay of Gibraltar. Algeciras is the terminus of two major European highways going via France and England all the way to Scotland - E05 (ends in Greenock ) and E15 (in Inverness ). Spanish highways serving the city include Autopista AP-7 (Autopista del Mediterraneo/tall motorway along Spain's Mediterranean coast/La Jonquera-Algeciras), Autovia A-48 (Cadiz-Algeciras), N-340 (Cadiz-Barcelona) and GR-7 (links Spain with Andorra and France). The nearest airports are in Gibraltar (20 km / 12 mi), Jerez de la Frontera (100 km / 62 mi) and Malaga (120 km / 75 mi). Independent with some planning or transport. Central Algeciras is compact and suitable for a short walk, but cruise calls are uncommon and ships may use different berths within this large commercial port. Confirm the passenger exit and any shuttle arrangements on board. Gibraltar, beaches and nature areas require transport.
getting_from_port: Algeciras is primarily a ferry, cargo and container port rather than a purpose-built cruise destination. Walking inside operational areas may be restricted, so use any shuttle or designated passenger route provided for the call. From the public port or maritime-station area, Plaza Alta and the central shopping streets are approximately 1 km (0.6 mi) away. The intercity bus station on Calle San Bernardo is also close to the center. Taxis are the simplest option for Getares Beach, Parque del Centenario and Gibraltar.

things_to_do.name: Explore Central Algeciras
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for Plaza Alta, the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Palma, the small Sanctuary of Nuestra Señora de Europa, the Town Hall and Mercado Ingeniero Torroja. The center is lively and local rather than heavily touristic, with cafés and shops along the pedestrian streets. This is the easiest independent option, particularly for a short call or when the exact port exit is not known in advance.

things_to_do.name: Visit Gibraltar
things_to_do.description: Allow at least 5–7 hours. Gibraltar is roughly 25–30 km (15.5–18.6 mi) from Algeciras by road. Public buses run from Algeciras to La Línea de la Concepción, normally taking about 45 minutes; passengers then walk across the international border into Gibraltar. A taxi, private transfer or organized excursion is more practical when time is limited. Border queues, traffic and the additional journey from the frontier to Gibraltar’s main sights can substantially lengthen the outing. Carry the travel documents required for both Spain and Gibraltar and verify current entry requirements before leaving the ship. Organized excursion recommended for visits combining the Upper Rock, viewpoints and central Gibraltar, especially on a call shorter than eight hours.

things_to_do.name: Relax at Getares Beach
things_to_do.description: Getares is a semi-urban sandy beach approximately 5 km (3.1 mi) south of central Algeciras. It has a promenade and places to eat, with views toward the Strait and Gibraltar. Allow 3–4 hours including transport. A taxi is the most convenient choice for cruise visitors. Walking from the port is too time-consuming for an ordinary call. Swimming conditions and beach facilities are seasonal, and exposed weather can make a beach visit less appealing.

things_to_do.name: Parque del Centenario and Strait Views
things_to_do.description: This coastal park offers viewpoints over Algeciras Bay, the Strait of Gibraltar and, in clear weather, the North African coast. Paths cross uneven and occasionally sloping ground, so suitable footwear is useful. Combine it with Getares or the nearby coast on a taxi outing of approximately 2–3 hours. Independent with transport. Arrange a return taxi or confirm local transport before setting out, as the park is not a practical walk from most port exits.

things_to_do.name: Port to Plaza Alta and San Isidro
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 2.5 km (1.6 mi) as a circuit from the public port area Pure walking time: about 35–45 minutes Recommended time: 2–3 hours with stops Difficulty: Easy to moderate; mostly urban streets, with an incline toward San Isidro Passenger exit or shuttle drop-off: Follow the designated route out of the operational port. Mercado Ingeniero Torroja: Visit the distinctive circular market when it is open and browse the surrounding produce and food stalls. Plaza Alta: Pause in the tiled central square beside the Church of Nuestra Señora de la Palma. Sanctuary of Nuestra Señora de Europa: See the small chapel on the edge of Plaza Alta. Town Hall: Continue along the central streets to the municipal building. San Isidro: Walk uphill through this traditional neighborhood of narrow lanes and whitewashed houses. Parque María Cristina: Descend toward the city park before returning through the commercial center. Return directly to the confirmed shuttle point or passenger entrance. Do not attempt to re-enter the port through an unauthorized gate.
things_to_do.recommended_time: 2–3 hours with stops Difficulty: Easy to moderate

summary: Port Alghero cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. The port's schedule lists all ships (in links) with cruises going to or leaving from Alghero, Sardinia Italy. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link.
description: Port Alghero cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. The port's schedule lists all ships (in links) with cruises going to or leaving from Alghero, Sardinia Italy. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link. Alghero is a port town in Mediterranean Sea. It is located on Italy's Sardinia Island and in Sassari (an Italian insular province in the island's northwestern part). Alghero has population around 44,000, part of which descends from Catalan conquerors from the end of Middle Ages. Back then, Sardinia Island was part of the Kingdom of Aragon. That is why Catalan language is co-official in the town (unique in Italy), taking the name of algueres dialect. The city name itself comes from the medieval Latin word Aleguerium, which means stagnation of algae (Posidonia oceanica - seagrass species endemic to the Mediterranean Sea). Alghero is the 5th university center in the island, following Cagliari and Sassari. It hosts the headquarters of Universita degli Studi di Sassari’s Architecture and Design department. Alghero was the 10th most visited city by tourists in Italy in 2012. Alghero has total area approx 224 km2 (87 mi2). Ozieri culture was present during the 4th millennium BC (Necropolis of Anghelu Ruju), and Nuraghe civilization settled here around 1,500 BC. Historically, the city of Alghero was founded in the early 12th century between 1102-1112, when the aristocratic Doria family of Genoa was permitted to build the first ever historical nucleus into the empty coast of Nulauro parish in Judicature of Torres (Sassari). It's uncertain whether it was some prior settlement, probably linked to the events of Saracen invasions. The many historical dominances that occurred in Alghero have produced a wide variety of buildings, monuments and sights. From the Neolithic period with many settlements that still remain, up to nowadays, during the last decades the town has become a major tourist point not only due to its coast and natural beauty but also because of a well preserved patrimony. There is a fishing and pleasure port in the heart of Alghero. Passenger traffic is handled via Porto Torres , some 30 km (18,6 ml) north. From there, ferry services are offered to Barcelona , Civitavecchia and Genoa . Easy independently. Alghero is normally an anchorage port, with passengers transferred ashore by tender. Tenders usually arrive at the marina beside the historic center, placing the old town, waterfront and main sights within easy walking distance. The compact center suits a relaxed independent visit. Transport is needed for Neptune’s Grotto, the archaeological sites, Porto Conte and most beaches beyond the town waterfront.
getting_from_port: There is generally no need for a shuttle after landing. The old town begins beside the harbor, while the cathedral, defensive towers and seafront ramparts are approximately 5–15 minutes away on foot. Most central streets are pedestrian-friendly, but old paving stones, steps and uneven surfaces can make walking difficult for passengers with limited mobility. Taxis and local buses are useful for beaches and attractions outside Alghero. Because this is a tender port, rough seas can delay or prevent passengers from going ashore. Allow additional time for the return tender and follow the ship’s stated last-tender time.
tender_evidence: Alghero is normally an anchorage port, with passengers transferred ashore by tender.

things_to_do.name: Explore Alghero Old Town
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for the historic lanes, Cathedral of Santa Maria, Church of San Francesco, small squares and shops selling local coral jewelry. Continue along the waterfront walls for views across the bay. This is the easiest and most reliable independent option.

things_to_do.name: Walk the Ramparts and Waterfront
things_to_do.description: A shorter visit can combine the harbor, Torre di Porta Terra, the sea walls and the Bastioni Marco Polo promenade. The route is scenic and close to the tender landing, making it suitable when time ashore is limited.

things_to_do.name: Visit Neptune’s Grotto
things_to_do.description: Boat trips normally leave from Alghero harbor and provide the most convenient independent route to the cave. Allow roughly half a day, including the cruise along the coast and the cave visit. Boat operations and cave access depend on wind and sea conditions, so confirm departures after arriving and avoid an option that returns too close to the final tender. The alternative is a road transfer to Capo Caccia followed by the Escala del Cabirol, a cliffside staircase of about 660 steps each way. This version is physically demanding and requires carefully coordinated transport. A ship excursion or organized local tour is preferable when the port call is short.

things_to_do.name: Nuraghe Palmavera and Porto Conte
things_to_do.description: The Nuraghe Palmavera archaeological complex is about 10 km (6.2 mi) northwest of Alghero. It can be combined with coastal scenery or Porto Conte, but transport is required. A taxi or organized excursion is more practical than relying on infrequent regional buses during a cruise call.

things_to_do.name: Easy Old Town and Ramparts Circuit
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 2 km (1.2 mi). Pure walking time: about 30 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy, with uneven paving and occasional steps. Start at the marina tender landing and walk toward Piazza Civica. Continue through the old lanes to the Cathedral of Santa Maria. Reach the seafront at Torre di Sant’Elmo. Follow the ramparts toward Bastioni Marco Polo. Turn inland for the Church of San Francesco and its surrounding lanes. Pass Torre di Porta Terra, once a principal entrance to the fortified town. Return through the shopping streets and harbor promenade to the tender landing. The route remains close to the harbor throughout and can be shortened easily. Passengers who find cobblestones difficult can concentrate on the harbor and wider rampart promenade.
things_to_do.difficulty: easy, with uneven paving and occasional steps

things_to_do.name: Moderate Old Town and Coastal Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 5 km (3.1 mi) round trip. Pure walking time: 70–80 minutes. Recommended total time: 3–4 hours. Difficulty: moderate because of the longer distance, sun exposure and uneven old-town paving. Follow the easy old-town circuit to Bastioni Marco Polo. Continue south along the waterfront toward the seafront promenade. Walk as far as the Las Tronas coastal area for open views back toward the fortified town. Return by the same waterfront route or use parallel streets through the modern center. Finish at the marina with ample time for the return tender. This route is better for passengers interested in scenery than indoor attractions. There is limited shade on parts of the waterfront.
things_to_do.difficulty: moderate because of the longer distance, sun exposure and uneven old-town paving

things_to_do.name: San Giovanni and Lido Beach
things_to_do.description: The nearest practical sandy shoreline lies north of the harbor, beginning roughly 1.5 km (0.9 mi) from the old town. It is reachable on foot along the waterfront and works well for a brief swim combined with sightseeing.

things_to_do.name: Maria Pia Beach
things_to_do.description: Maria Pia is approximately 4 km (2.5 mi) north of the historic center and is known for pale sand, shallow water and a pine-backed shoreline. Use a taxi or check the current local bus service rather than spending much of a short call walking there. Allow extra return time during the busy summer season.

Algiers (port locode DZALG) is the principal/largest port and the capital city of Algeria, with urban population around 3,5 million and metro population around 5 million. The city is located in North Africa (Maghreb region, on the Mediterranean Sea), in Algeria's north-central portion. It covers a total area of approx 363 km2 (140 mi2). Sometimes nicknamed "El-Behdja" or "Algiers the White" (Alger la Blanche) for the sparkling white of its buildings as seen rising from the sea, Algiers is located on the west side of a bay in the Mediterranean Sea. The city's modern part is built on level ground by the seashore. The ancient city of deys (the old part), climbs the hill behind the contemporary town and is crowned by the citadel (casbah), 122 m (400 ft) above sea level. The citadel and the two quays make a triangle. Algiers is a major economic, financial and commercial center, with a stock exchange featuring a capitalization of EUR 60 million. Algiers has the highest living cost of any North African city. There are a wealth of public buildings of interest in Algiers, including the whole quarter of Kasbah, Sahat ech-Chouhada (Martyrs Square), the government offices (former British consulate), the "New", "Grand", and Ketchaoua Mosques, the Bardo Museum (former Turkish mansion), the Roman Catholic cathedral of Notre Dame d'Afrique, the old Bibliotheque Nationale d'Alger (Turkish palace built 1799–1800), as well as the new National Library (in a style reminiscent of British Library). Some 20 km (12 ml) to the west of Algiers are popular seaside resorts, including Sidi Fredj (former Sidi Ferruch), Douaouda, Zeralda, Palm Beach, and Club of the Pines (residence of State). Other amenities include tourist complexes, supervised beaches, souvenir shops, Algerian and other restaurants. The city of Algiers is also equipped with famous hotel complexes like Hilton Hotel, El Djazair and El-Aurassi. It also boasts the first water park in Algeria. The tourism industry is growing but is not as developed as that of larger cities in Tunisia or Morocco. Independent with some planning or transport. Cruise ships normally dock in Algiers' commercial port rather than tendering. The waterfront, Place des Martyrs and Lower Casbah are close to the port, but the permitted passenger exit and freedom to explore independently can vary by ship and local security arrangements. Confirm onboard whether passengers may leave independently or must use an approved transfer or excursion. If independent visits are permitted, central Algiers is manageable on foot and by metro. A guide is strongly recommended for the Upper Casbah.
getting_from_port: On foot: Place des Martyrs and the lower edge of the Casbah may be within approximately 15–25 minutes of the passenger exit. The exact distance depends on the berth and internal port arrangements. Shuttle: Use a cruise-line shuttle if one is provided, particularly because walking may not be permitted through operational sections of the port. Taxi: Useful for Notre-Dame d'Afrique, the Martyrs' Memorial and other hilltop sights. Agree on the fare or confirm that the meter will be used before departing. Metro: Place des Martyrs station serves the historic center. Jardin d'Essai station provides convenient access to the botanical garden and the cable-car connection toward the Martyrs' Memorial area. Check the current operating schedule locally.
tender_evidence: Cruise ships normally dock in Algiers' commercial port rather than tendering.

things_to_do.name: Lower Casbah and Central Algiers
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for Place des Martyrs, the exterior of Ketchaoua Mosque, the lower lanes of the UNESCO-listed Casbah and the arcaded streets of the French-era center. This is the simplest independent option when passengers are allowed to leave the port freely. The Lower Casbah can be explored cautiously from its main approaches, but the old quarter becomes steep and confusing higher up. Avoid attempting an improvised route deep into the Upper Casbah.

things_to_do.name: Guided Casbah Visit
things_to_do.description: Allow approximately 3–4 hours. A licensed guide can lead a mostly downhill route through the Upper Casbah, explaining buildings that are easy to miss and navigating the maze of alleys, stairs and passages. This is the preferred choice for a first visit and for anyone wanting more than a short look at the lower district. The route requires secure footwear and confidence on uneven paving and numerous steps. It is unsuitable for wheelchairs and difficult for passengers with limited mobility.

things_to_do.name: Jardin d'Essai and the Martyrs' Memorial
things_to_do.description: Allow 3–4 hours. Travel by metro or taxi to Jardin d'Essai du Hamma, a large botanical garden with broad shaded avenues. Continue toward the hilltop Martyrs' Memorial by cable car when operating, or use a taxi. The memorial area provides wide views over Algiers and the bay. This combination is practical independently if port rules allow and local transport is operating normally. A taxi is the easier alternative when time is limited or cable-car service is unavailable.

things_to_do.name: Panoramic City Tour
things_to_do.description: Allow 4–5 hours for a guided or private-vehicle circuit combining Notre-Dame d'Afrique, the Martyrs' Memorial, Jardin d'Essai and selected central landmarks. The basilica and memorial both occupy elevated sites, so combining them by vehicle saves considerable climbing and travel time. This option works well for passengers with limited mobility, although individual attractions may still involve steps and sloping paths.

things_to_do.name: Tipasa Archaeological Excursion
things_to_do.description: Tipasa lies approximately 68 km (42.3 mi) west of Algiers, normally at least one hour away by road in each direction. Its coastal archaeological site contains Punic, Roman and early Christian remains. Organized excursion recommended. A visit normally needs 6–8 hours once transfers and sightseeing are included. Traffic can lengthen the return journey, making independent public transport unsuitable for most cruise calls.

things_to_do.name: Place des Martyrs and the Colonial Center
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 3.5 km (2.2 mi). Pure walking time: about 50–60 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy to moderate, with busy pavements, road crossings and some gradients. Passenger exit or shuttle stop: Confirm the required return point and latest reboarding time before setting out. Place des Martyrs: Begin at the broad waterfront square between the port and the old city. Ketchaoua Mosque: View the prominent mosque at the foot of the Casbah. Enter only if visitors are being admitted and observe local dress and worship rules. Lower Casbah: Make a short circuit through the busier lower lanes without climbing deep into the maze of the Upper Casbah. Place Emir Abdelkader: Continue through the central commercial streets to this busy city square. Grande Poste: See the landmark Neo-Moorish post-office building and the surrounding boulevards. Waterfront return: Walk back toward Place des Martyrs and follow the ship's specified route or shuttle instructions to the port. This route should be shortened if the assigned passenger exit is farther inside the port than expected. Keep valuables unobtrusive and take normal precautions in crowded streets.
things_to_do.difficulty: easy to moderate, with busy pavements, road crossings and some gradients

Algoma WI (port locode USAGM ) is a Lake Michigan cruise port and town in Wisconsin USA (Kewaunee County) with population around 3,000. Algoma is at the Ahnapee River's mouth and is road-connected with Sturgeon Bay (via highway WIS 42) to the north and with Kewaunee to the south, as well as with Green Bay (via highway WIS 54) to the west. Watercraft (boats, yachts and cruise ships) dock at Hill Pier 42 Marina. Being one of the Great Lakes , Lake Michigan has surface area (22300 mi2/58000 km2), water volume (1180 mi3/4900 km3) max depth (925 ft/282 m), cities in Illinois ( Chicago ), Indiana (Gary), Wisconsin ( Green Bay , Sheboygan, Milwaukee , Kenosha, Racine) and Michigan ( Muskegon , Traverse City ). Currently, the largest by capacity Great Lakes cruise companies are Viking Cruises USA (ships Viking Octantis , Viking Polaris ), AQV-American Queen Voyages (ships Ocean Navigator , Ocean Voyager ), Pearl Seas Cruises ( Pearl Mist ), and the Canadian company St Lawrence Cruise Lines ( Canadian Empress ). Other travel brands that offer Great Lakes voyages are PONANT and Tauck ( fleet ). Algoma WI's most popular tourist activities include sports fishing, sailing, leisure boating, trailing, Since 2000, the town holds annually the Algoma Car Show (in June, showcasing classical cars and trucks), Shanty Days Fair (in August, presenting foods, draft beer, wine tasting, live music, arts and crafts show, fireworks, parade) and The Park Concerts Series (in July-August). The settlement was established in the mid-19th-century (1834). The town (as Wolf River) was founded in 1851, renamed Ahnapee in 1859, incorporated in 1879, and renamed Algoma in 1897. One of the town's major industries was commercial fishing, having the largest fishing fleet on Lake Michigan. Algoma started to develop following the integration into A&W (Ahnapee and Western Railway, length 35 mi / 56 km) which interconnected Sturgeon Bay (northern terminus), Maplewood, Forestville, Algoma, Casco, Kewaunee, Green Bay (southern/western terminus). Part of the historic A&W railroad is the current-day Ahnapee State Trail - a multi-purpose trail for activities like hiking, biking, horse riding, and snowmobiling. The trail runs the former Green Bay and Western Railroad's line from Casco Junction to Sturgeon Bay. Independent with some planning. Algoma is a compact, walkable Lake Michigan town. Once ashore, passengers can independently explore Crescent Beach, the waterfront and downtown without needing a vehicle. Longer trips into Door County are better suited to an organized excursion. Cruise ships normally remain offshore because the harbor cannot accommodate large expedition vessels. Tenders bring passengers into the Algoma marina area near Heritage Park and downtown. The exact landing point and passenger arrangements can vary by call. Most local attractions are within a short walk of the waterfront, so taxis are unnecessary for exploring Algoma itself. Tender operations may be slowed or changed by Lake Michigan conditions; allow extra time for the return trip and follow the ship’s stated last-tender time.
terminal_notes: Watercraft (boats, yachts and cruise ships) dock at Hill Pier 42 Marina.
tender_evidence: Tenders bring passengers into the Algoma marina area near Heritage Park and downtown.

things_to_do.name: Crescent Beach and Boardwalk
things_to_do.description: This is Algoma’s easiest independent outing. The public lakefront park includes a sandy beach, grassy areas, benches and an accessible boardwalk approximately 0.8 km (0.5 mi) long. Allow 45–90 minutes for a relaxed shoreline walk, photography or beachcombing. Lake Michigan water can remain cold even in summer, and conditions may be windy.

things_to_do.name: Downtown Murals, Shops and Galleries
things_to_do.description: Algoma’s compact center contains outdoor historical murals, small galleries, independent shops and places for refreshments. A self-guided mural brochure may be available from the Algoma Visitor Center. Allow approximately 1–2 hours; this is easy to combine with the beach and waterfront.

things_to_do.name: Ahnapee River Waterfront and Local Tasting
things_to_do.description: Walk along the harbor and lower Ahnapee River, then visit downtown businesses or the historic von Stiehl Winery. Tastings and tours depend on the day’s operating schedule, so confirm availability before relying on them. This option is practical independently and usually requires 1–2 hours.

things_to_do.name: Ahnapee State Trail
things_to_do.description: The Ahnapee State Trail provides a mostly level, firm-surface route through the river corridor and surrounding countryside. Cruise visitors should treat it as an out-and-back walk rather than attempt a distant destination. A short section of 3–6 km (1.9–3.7 mi) can fit into a port call, with approximately 1–2 hours required.

things_to_do.name: Door County
things_to_do.description: Algoma can serve as a gateway to the Door Peninsula. Sturgeon Bay is roughly a 20–30-minute drive away, while Peninsula State Park and the bay-side villages require considerably more travel. A broad Door County highlights trip commonly occupies about five hours or longer. There is no practical public transport for a flexible sightseeing circuit from the tender landing. An organized excursion is recommended because it coordinates transportation and return timing. Passengers on shorter calls should remain in Algoma rather than attempt the northern peninsula independently.

name: Aliaga Ship Breaking Yard (Turkey)
summary: Aliaga (port locode TRALI) is an Eastern Mediterranean/Aegean Sea port town in Turkey's Izmir Province, with population around 60,000. Aliaga is approx 50 km (31 mi) north of the province's capital Izmir .
description: Aliaga (port locode TRALI) is an Eastern Mediterranean/Aegean Sea port town in Turkey's Izmir Province, with population around 60,000. Aliaga is approx 50 km (31 mi) north of the province's capital Izmir . Port Aliaga (locode TRALI) serves mainly oil tankers and bulk cargo ships. The region's economy is based on tourism, shipbreaking, crude oil processing (petroleum refinery). Aliaga Ship Breaking Yard houses several facilities used for dismantling and scrapping of mainly passenger ships ( ferries and cruise liners). The cruise shipbreaking increased due to the Coronavirus crisis, and especially in 2020-2021, when shipowners sold for scrap some of their fleets' oldest vessels that were idled/in cold layups and losing money. By capacity and annual scrapped DWT-deadweight tonnage, Aliaga is currently ranked the world's fourth-largest shipbreaking facility - following Alang (India) , Chittagong (Bangladesh) and Gadani (Pakistan) . Next are listed the most famous ocean liners (SS), ferries and cruise vessels scrapped at Aliaga. In brackets is shown the boat's year-built and year-scrapped. Currently awaiting with a most uncertain future (located in Greece, "close to Aliaga" and awaiting scrapping) are the passenger ships Marella Celebration (1984), Pullmantur Horizon (1990), Pullmantur Zenith (1992), Majesty of the Seas (1992). The list of the scrapped ship's former owners includes Carnival Corporation (via the subsidiaries CCL-Carnival , Costa , Princess ), Royal Caribbean Group (via Pullmantur, RCI-Royal Caribbean International ), NCLH (via NCL-Norwegian Cruise Line ), Fred Olsen , CMV-Cruise and Maritime Voyages (2010-founded/2020-defunct), Portuscale Cruises (2013-founded/2021-defunct), Epirotiki Line (1850-founded/2005-defunct). Note: Due to the Coronavirus crisis and IMO's new regulations (marine engine upgrades for using low-sulfur fuels and LNG ), in 2020-2021 were scrapped 15 cruise liners - an unprecedented number in comparison to previous years, and even 5-year periods. In 2020, the average ship scrap metal (DWT-deadweight tonnage) prices in Alang rose to ~USD 400 per ton (from ~$200), in Aliaga - to ~USD 300 per ton (from ~$100). EU- flagged ships' scrap values were ~USD 100-200 per ton as these vessels require dismantling at EU-certified yards. Ship scrap prices in the USA were USD 80-90 per ton. Independent sightseeing is not possible. Aliağa Ship Breaking Yard is an active industrial ship-recycling area rather than a cruise terminal. Passenger ships listed here normally arrive at the end of their service lives for dismantling, not on scheduled cruise calls. There is no cruise terminal, tender landing, shuttle service or authorized passenger exit associated with the ship-breaking yard. The recycling facilities are controlled workplaces with heavy machinery and significant safety hazards. Visitors should not attempt to enter the yards or approach them on foot. Arrivals shown for this location generally record vessels being delivered for recycling. They should not be interpreted as opportunities to embark, disembark or visit Aliağa during a cruise. Because this is not a passenger port of call, self-guided walking tours, beaches and shore excursions are not applicable. Travelers visiting the wider Aliağa area independently should arrange their plans from the town itself and remain outside restricted port and industrial zones. Alicante (aka Alacant/both are official city names) is a port city in Spain on Costa Blanca, as well as the capital of Alicante Province and of Alacanti comarca. Alicante is also a major Mediterranean port (cargo and ferry), with city population around 330,000. By population (around 760,000), Alicante Metro is ranked Spain's 8th-largest. By annual passenger shipping traffic, Alicante is one of Spain's major ports (for both cruise vessels and ferries ), with more than 70 calls/visits by cruise ships and estimated 100,000+ passengers plus 40,000+ crew annually. Studies show that the average expenditure per cruise tourist is EUR 300+, including expenses on hotels, shopping, and excursions (before/after the voyage). Port Alicante (locode ESALC) serves regularly scheduled ferry connections linking Spain with Algeria ( Oran , Algiers , Mostaganem) and the Balearic Islands (Mallorca), the latter route being operated from Denia (to the northeast of Alicante). In December 2022, Global Ports Holding (UK-based cruise port operator company/currently ranked the world's largest) announced winning the public tender and being awarded by the Alicante Port Authority a 15-year concession of Alicante Cruise Port (2023 thru 2038). The facility is operated via a joint venture consortium (80:20) between Global Ports Holding and Sepcan SL Maritime (Servicios Portuarios Canarios). The port concession deal was signed in March 2023. In 2023, the Port reported a record year with scheduled 86 cruise ship calls and estimated 200,000+ tourists. The booked berthings included both stopovers and homeporting (embarkation/debarkation). In 2023, MSC Cruises increased/doubled its homeport operations by basing here two liners ( MSC Lirica , MSC Orchestra ) for a total of 25 roundtrip voyages out of Alicante. Of the 86 visits, 7 were maiden - by cruise ships making their inaugural calls in Alicante. Among the city's most notable features are Castell de Santa Barbara (9th-century castle on Mt Benacantil, overlooking the city) and the Port. The latter was a subject of controversy in 2006–2007 as the residents successfully battled to keep it from being changed into an industrial estate. Santa Barbara Castle's La Torreta Tower is its oldest part, while the walls and part of the lowest zone were constructed during the 18th century. The promenade Explanada de Espana is lined by palm trees and paved with 6.5M marble floor tiles that create a wavy form. The Promenade is one of the most beautiful promenades in Spain and extends from Port of Alicante to Gran Vía, ending at the statue of Mark Hersch. For Alicante's residents, Explanada de Espana is the meeting place for traditional Spanish paseo, or evening stroll along the waterfront, and a venue for musical concerts. At its end is a monument by the artist Banuls of the 19th century. Just a few kilometers from the city is Tabarca Island. Once a haven for Barbary pirates, today it is a beautiful tourist attraction. Easy independently. Cruise ships dock at Alicante Cruise Terminal, about 1 km (0.6 mi) from the city center. Alicante’s waterfront, historic center, Santa Bárbara Castle and Postiguet Beach are all close enough to combine during a typical port call.
getting_from_port: Ships normally berth at the outer Levante piers. The exact walking distance depends on the berth, but passengers can usually reach the marina and city waterfront in about 15–25 minutes. A port shuttle generally operates between the cruise terminal and the waterfront near the city center. Service arrangements can vary by call, so confirm the drop-off point and final return time onboard. Taxis may also be available at the terminal. From the waterfront, the Explanada de España, old town and Postiguet Beach are readily accessible on foot. Alicante’s buses and TRAM are more useful for beaches and neighborhoods outside the center than for the main central sights.
terminal_notes: Cruise ships dock at Alicante Cruise Terminal, about 1 km (0.6 mi) from the city center.
tender_evidence: In December 2022, Global Ports Holding (UK-based cruise port operator company/currently ranked the world's largest) announced winning the public tender and being awarded by the Alicante Port Authority a 15-year concession of Alicante Cruise Port (2023 thru 2038).

things_to_do.name: Old Town and Waterfront
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for the Explanada de España, Town Hall area, San Nicolás Co-Cathedral, Santa María Basilica and the narrow streets of the historic center. Most of this area is compact and pedestrian-friendly, although the Santa Cruz neighborhood contains steep lanes and steps.

things_to_do.name: Santa Bárbara Castle
things_to_do.description: Allow about 2–3 hours including access and sightseeing. The castle stands above the city on Mount Benacantil and offers broad views over Alicante and the coast. The easiest approach is via the lift entrance on Avenida Juan Bautista Lafora, opposite Postiguet Beach, or by the castle minibus when operating. Walking to the summit is possible but involves a sustained uphill climb, uneven surfaces and steps. Check current lift or minibus operation before setting out.

things_to_do.name: Postiguet Beach
things_to_do.description: This central urban beach lies beside the old town and below the castle, making it practical for a short swim or a relaxed waterfront stop. Allow 1–3 hours. It is much easier to combine with sightseeing than the more distant beaches along the coast.

things_to_do.name: Museums and Local Culture
things_to_do.description: The Contemporary Art Museum of Alicante is close to Santa María Basilica, while the archaeological museum, MARQ, is farther north of the old town. The Ocean Race Museum is particularly convenient near the marina and can fit into a shorter call. Verify opening days and admission arrangements before relying on a museum visit.

things_to_do.name: Tabarca Island
things_to_do.description: Boats from Alicante generally take about one hour each way. A visit usually requires around 6 hours including the crossings, so it is suitable only for a long port call with well-matched seasonal boat times. Because departures can be limited and sea conditions may affect service, this is less reliable than staying in Alicante.

things_to_do.name: Easy Waterfront and Old Town Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 3 km (1.9 mi). Pure walking time: about 45 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy, mostly level. Start at the port shuttle stop or marina entrance. Walk along the palm-lined Explanada de España. Continue to Alicante Town Hall and the surrounding old-town streets. Visit San Nicolás Co-Cathedral. Walk to Santa María Basilica and the nearby Contemporary Art Museum. Continue to Postiguet Beach. Return along the waterfront to the shuttle stop or port entrance. This route is suitable for most visitors. Cobblestones and short inclines occur within the old town, but the waterfront sections are largely flat.

things_to_do.name: Castle and Santa Cruz Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 5 km (3.1 mi), excluding any shuttle ride from the berth. Pure walking time: about 1 hour 30 minutes. Recommended total time: 3–4 hours. Difficulty: moderate to challenging, with steep lanes and many steps. Start at the marina and walk beside Postiguet Beach. Use the castle lift if operating, or climb by a signed pedestrian route. Explore Santa Bárbara Castle and its viewpoints. Descend through La Ereta Park. Continue through the hillside Santa Cruz neighborhood. Visit Santa María Basilica and the Town Hall area. Return via the Explanada de España. The Santa Cruz section is accessible only on foot and is unsuitable for some visitors with limited mobility. Using the lift for the ascent reduces the effort but does not remove the steep descent, steps and uneven paving.
things_to_do.difficulty: moderate to challenging, with steep lanes and many steps

Aljmas (port locode HRALJ) is a Danube River cruise port and village in Croatia's Osijek-Baranja County (eastern Slavonia) and part of the Erdut municipality, with a population of under 1,000. Erdut is located approx 37 km (23 mi) east of Osijek (on the Croatia-Serbia border). Aljmas is among the pilgrimage destinations in Croatia, being visited by around 100,000 tourists arriving here each year on August 15 to celebrate Virgin Mary's assumption into Heaven. As a cruise port, Aljmas was added in the nickoVISION ship's 2019 schedule from homeport Passau. The next table shows the 14-day itinerary's ports and port times (arrival/departure). Prices started from USD 1240 pp (double occupancy rates). Independent with some planning or transport. Aljmaš is a small Danube village rather than a conventional city port. Its church, riverfront and village streets are easily explored on foot, but the surrounding wineries, Erdut, Osijek and Kopački Rit Nature Park require arranged transport or an organized excursion. River ships use the local Aljmaš berth, placing passengers close to the compact village. There is no large cruise terminal, and the central sights are generally reached on foot. The exact gangway location can vary with river conditions, so follow the ship's directions when going ashore. Do not depend on finding taxis at the berth. Arrange transport through the ship or in advance for any trip beyond the village. Public transport is not practical for a short port call.

things_to_do.name: Explore Aljmaš on Foot
things_to_do.description: Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for the village's main sights. The centerpiece is the modern Church and Sanctuary of Our Lady of Refuge, often called the Danube Swan because of its distinctive shape. When accessible, its memorial collection provides useful context about the destruction and rebuilding of the sanctuary. Continue along the quiet riverside and through the neighboring streets for views across the Danube. Aljmaš is small, so this option is easy to manage independently without filling the entire port call.

things_to_do.name: Climb the Stations of the Cross
things_to_do.description: A hillside path follows 14 carved Stations of the Cross for approximately 500 m (0.3 mi), ending near a large statue and an elevated viewpoint. The climb adds about 45–75 minutes to a village walk. Expect an uphill surface and wear shoes with good grip; it may not suit passengers with limited mobility.

things_to_do.name: Visit Erdut and Its Wine Country
things_to_do.description: The Erdut peninsula combines vineyards, Danube viewpoints, wineries and the remains of a medieval tower above the river. Some wineries accept visitors only by prior arrangement, especially outside weekday hours, so this is best booked as a guided outing or prearranged taxi tour. Allow about 3–4 hours, including transport and a tasting. Wine tastings should never be assumed to accept walk-in visitors. Confirm arrangements before leaving Aljmaš.

things_to_do.name: Discover Osijek
things_to_do.description: Osijek lies approximately 26 km (16.2 mi) west of Aljmaš. Its principal visitor area includes the Baroque Tvrđa quarter, Holy Trinity Square and the long Drava riverfront promenade. Allow roughly 4–5 hours for the transfer and a focused city visit. Independent travel is possible with transport reserved in advance, but a ship excursion is simpler because local taxis and return connections cannot be assumed.

things_to_do.name: Explore Kopački Rit Nature Park
things_to_do.description: This extensive wetland near the Drava–Danube confluence is known for birdlife, waterways and floodplain scenery. Visits can combine the visitor center, the White Water-Lily boardwalk and a scheduled boat experience. Organized excursion recommended. The park is outside Aljmaš, its activities operate to set schedules, and reservations are required for visitor programs. Allow at least half a day and check which experiences are included in the tour.

things_to_do.name: Riverfront, Sanctuary and Calvary
things_to_do.description: Suggested route: river berth – Aljmaš waterfront – Church of Our Lady of Refuge – village center – Stations of the Cross – viewpoint – return through the village to the ship. Approximate distance: 2–3 km (1.2–1.9 mi), depending on the berth and how far you continue along the waterfront. Pure walking time: about 40–60 minutes. Recommended total time: 1.5–2.5 hours with church, memorial and viewpoint stops. Difficulty: easy within the village; moderate if the uphill Calvary path is included. Return: retrace the village streets to the river berth, allowing extra time if another tour group is using the gangway. Passengers wanting a gentler route can omit the Calvary and remain around the church and riverfront.

Alken is a Moselle River cruise port, town and municipality in Germany's Rhineland-Palatinate state (Mayen-Koblenz district) with population of around 1000. Alken features a number of old houses and remains of medieval walls. Major sights of interest in the village include Laacher Yard, which is one of the oldest buildings (it dates back from 1093), the Fallertor (City Gate) from 1256, the military tower (also from 1256) and Malteserhaus, one of the village's oldest houses. From here travelers can also explore Ahr Valley, one of the most picturesque of Rhine's tributary valleys. On a hill spur above the village stand Thurant Castle's ruins. The castle is situated within Mayen-Koblenz county in Rhineland-Palatinate state and belongs to spur castle type. Next to Thurant Castle which stands on the valley's steep shoulder, on the sunny side are spread vast vine gardens. From the mid-13th-century, the archbishops of Trier and Cologne were joint owners of the castle's site and had their property managed by burgraves. Each half of the castle, as a result, had its own bergfried, domestic and living buildings, as well as a separate entrance. From the beginning of the 16th century, this unique double castle slowly fell into disrepair and was turned into a complete ruin during destruction wrought by War of the Palatine Succession. In 1911, Robert Allmers (1872–1951) from Varel, co-founder of Hansa Automobil company and Director of Bremen's Hansa Lloyd factories from 1914, purchased the site and had part of it rebuilt. Today the castle is still in private hands but maybe visited from March until mid-November for a fee. It is a protected monument incorporated into the state monument list according to the Heritage Monument Conservation Act of Rhineland-Palatinate. The entire site was declared a protected zone. Thurant Castle is also a protected cultural object under the Hague Convention and displays blue and white protection signs. Independent sightseeing: Easy for the riverside village; independent with planning and good mobility for Thurant Castle. Alken is a compact Moselle wine village beneath Thurant Castle. River ships normally stop close to the village, so no transfer is usually needed. A short call is enough for the historic lanes and waterfront, while the castle requires a steep uphill walk. Passenger vessels use a landing stage on Alken’s Moselle waterfront. The promenade, restaurants and historic center are within a few minutes’ walk. Exact docking positions can change, but the village is small and practical to explore on foot. There is little reason to use public transport for Alken itself. A taxi may be useful for passengers who want to visit Thurant Castle without making the steep climb, although availability should be arranged in advance or through the ship.

things_to_do.name: Explore Historic Alken
things_to_do.description: Allow 45–90 minutes for the Moselle promenade and the village’s old lanes. Look for half-timbered wine houses, remnants of the medieval fortifications, the Fallertor gate, the former defensive tower beside the river and the parish church. This is the easiest independent option and is mostly level near the waterfront.

things_to_do.name: Climb to Thurant Castle
things_to_do.description: Allow approximately 2–3 hours for the uphill walk, castle visit and return. The route rises through the village and vineyards, with steep sections and limited shade. Sturdy footwear is advisable. The privately owned double castle contains courtyards, towers, gardens and viewpoints over the Moselle. It is generally open seasonally rather than throughout the year, so confirm current access before starting. Passengers with limited mobility should consider a prearranged taxi and note that parts of the castle still involve uneven surfaces and steps.

things_to_do.name: Walk to Old St. Michael’s Church
things_to_do.description: The old church stands above the village and is reached by a picturesque but steep staircase marked by Stations of the Cross. Allow about 45–75 minutes from the waterfront for the climb, exterior views and return. Interior opening is limited and should not be assumed, but the elevated setting and views make the walk worthwhile.

things_to_do.name: Sample Moselle Wine
things_to_do.description: Alken has local wine estates and seasonal places serving regional Riesling. This works well as a relaxed addition to a village walk, but tasting availability varies. Use a venue close to the waterfront when the ship’s call is short.

things_to_do.name: Easy Village and Waterfront Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: Approximately 2 km (1.2 mi) Pure walking time: 30–40 minutes Recommended time: 1–1.5 hours Difficulty: Easy, with mostly level streets and a few cobbled or uneven sections. Start at the river landing stage and follow the Moselle promenade. See the old riverside defensive tower. Turn into the village lanes near Moselstraße. Pass the parish church and traditional wine houses. Continue to the medieval Fallertor gate and surviving wall sections. Return through Oberstraße and the historic center to the waterfront. The route remains close to the ship and can easily be shortened.
things_to_do.difficulty: Easy, with mostly level streets and a few cobbled or uneven sections

things_to_do.name: Moderate Castle and Old Church Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: Approximately 4 km (2.5 mi) round trip Pure walking time: 75–100 minutes Recommended time: 2.5–3 hours with visits Difficulty: Moderate to demanding because of sustained climbs, stairs and uneven vineyard paths. Start at the landing stage and walk through Alken’s historic center. Pass the Fallertor and follow signs toward Burg Thurant. Climb through the vineyard landscape to Thurant Castle. Visit the castle if it is open and enjoy the Moselle viewpoints. Descend toward Old St. Michael’s Church, using only clearly marked paths. Continue down the Stations of the Cross staircase into Alken. Return to the landing stage along the waterfront. Allow additional time after rain, when steep paths and stone steps may be slippery. If the ship’s stay is under three hours, choose either the castle or the old church rather than attempting the complete route.
things_to_do.difficulty: Moderate to demanding because of sustained climbs, stairs and uneven vineyard paths

name: Alkmaar (Netherlands North Holland)
summary: Alkmaar (port locode NLALK) is a North Holland Canal (river) cruise port, city and municipality in the Netherlands's North Holland province, with population around 110,000. The closest to Alkmaar "cruise cities" are Hoorn (east) and IJmuiden (southwest).
description: Alkmaar (port locode NLALK) is a North Holland Canal (river) cruise port, city and municipality in the Netherlands's North Holland province, with population around 110,000. The closest to Alkmaar "cruise cities" are Hoorn (east) and IJmuiden (southwest). The town is best-known among foreign and domestic tourists for its outdoor cheese market (open April through September on the Waagplein). The settlement was founded in the 10th century and in 1254 received its city rights. In August-October 1573 (during the 80 Years War / 1568-1648 between Spain and the revolting Holland, Belgium, and Luxembourg) the town was sieged by Spanish forces. The town was interlinked via Noordhollandsch Kanaal (1824), Alkmaar-Den Helder railway (1865) and Alkmaar-Haarlem railway (1867). The A9 highway links with Amsterdam and Den Helder . Noordhollandsch Kanaal (North-Holland Canal) has length approx 75 km (47 mi) and links Den Helder (north) with Amsterdam (south) via Alkmaar and Purmerend. This inland waterway was built (dug) in the period 1820-24 to shorten the sea access to Amsterdam City. However, due to vessels' increasing size (length, width, and draught) as well as the many bridges, sluices, and curves, the waterway soon became inadequate for seagoing ships. Plus, the canal's water freezes during the winter months. Noordzeekanaal (North Sea Canal) in 1865-76 linking directly Amsterdam with IJmuiden was built for this reason. Today, the North Holland Canal is used exclusively for commercial river shipping, recreational boating (yachts, hotel barges, cruise ships, tour boats) and water management. As a cruise port, Alkmaar is included in the regular schedule of one of Europe's largest river cruise companies - Nicko Cruises (brand of Mystic Cruises) . The next table shows the ports sequences of Nicko's Alkmaar-visiting itinerary (12-day "Holland and Germany") between homeports Amsterdam and Berlin. The cruisetour was operated by the riverboat MS Frederic Chopin and priced from ~USD 2700 pp. River cruise ships in Alkmaar berth directly in downtown. The town's 3 cruise docks can handle boats with max LOA lengths 130 m (Kanaalkade), 120 m (Noorderkade) and 90 m (Voormeer). Easy independently. River cruise ships berth beside the northern and eastern edges of central Alkmaar, and the compact historic district is readily explored on foot. Most visitors can walk from the quay to Waagplein, the canals, museums and shopping streets without needing a shuttle or taxi. River vessels may use Kanaalkade, Noorderkade or Voormeer. Kanaalkade and Noorderkade are immediately beside the city center, while Voormeer is slightly farther east but remains within practical walking distance of the main sights. Alkmaar has simple quays rather than a large passenger terminal, so check the vessel's exact berth before setting out. The historic center has mostly level streets, although cobblestones, narrow lanes and canal bridges can make wheelchair or mobility-aid access uneven. Taxis are more useful for trips outside Alkmaar than for sightseeing within the old town.

things_to_do.name: Historic Center and Waagplein
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for a relaxed circuit through Waagplein, the narrow lanes around Fnidsen and Hekelstraat, the Mient canal, Langestraat and the Grote Kerk. This is the most practical choice for a short call and requires no transport.

things_to_do.name: Alkmaar Cheese Market
things_to_do.description: The traditional cheese market is held at Waagplein on selected mornings during the spring and summer season, with additional evening events on limited dates. It is a scheduled demonstration rather than a daily attraction, so verify that its date and time match the ship's call. Arrive early because the square can become crowded. When the market is not operating, visitors can still see the historic Waag building and consider the Dutch Cheese Museum inside. The Alkmaar Store tourist office is also located at Waagplein.

things_to_do.name: Canal Boat Trip
things_to_do.description: A small sightseeing boat provides a different view of Alkmaar's façades, drawbridges and narrow canals. Standard trips take about 45 minutes and normally depart near the Waag area. Some bridges are extremely low, and passengers may need to bend down as the boat passes beneath them. Confirm departure times after reaching the center rather than relying on a boat trip for a tightly timed visit.

things_to_do.name: Museums and Grote Kerk
things_to_do.description: The Stedelijk Museum Alkmaar is the main choice for local art and city history. It stands near the Grote Kerk, making the two easy to combine in approximately 1.5–2.5 hours. The Dutch Cheese Museum at Waagplein is smaller and better suited to a brief visit. Check same-day opening before planning around either museum or the church.

things_to_do.name: Countryside, Windmills or the Coast
things_to_do.description: The polders, villages and North Sea coast around Alkmaar are better suited to a guided excursion, taxi tour or carefully planned bicycle trip. Possible regional destinations include the Schermer windmill landscape, De Rijp, Egmond aan Zee and the Schoorl dunes. These are not sensible additions to a very short call, and public-transport journeys require extra allowance for connections and delays.

things_to_do.name: Easy Old Town Circuit
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 3 km (1.9 mi). Pure walking time: about 45 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy, with occasional cobblestones and small canal bridges. Cruise quay: Walk toward the historic center from Kanaalkade, Noorderkade or Voormeer. Waagplein: See the Waag building and the setting of the seasonal cheese market. De Mient: Follow the canal past historic façades and waterside terraces. Fnidsen and Hekelstraat: Explore the compact old-quarter lanes and independent shops. Langestraat: Cross the principal pedestrian shopping street toward the Grote Kerk. Grote Kerk: View the large late-Gothic church and nearby cultural quarter. Return: Walk through the center to the appropriate quay, allowing time to locate the correct vessel entrance.
things_to_do.difficulty: easy, with occasional cobblestones and small canal bridges

things_to_do.name: Extended Monuments and Canals Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 4.5 km (2.8 mi). Pure walking time: about 1 hour. Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours. Difficulty: easy to moderate because of the longer distance, cobbles and bridges. Begin at the cruise quay and continue to Waagplein. Walk through the old lanes around Fnidsen and the Visbanken. Continue toward the Accijnstoren beside the water. Follow the green edge of the old center toward Molen van Piet. Visit the Grote Kerk and adjacent museum quarter. Return through Langestraat and the Mient canal area to the ship. This route follows the character of Alkmaar's official monuments walk. A route description or city map may be available from the tourist office in the Waag.
things_to_do.difficulty: easy to moderate because of the longer distance, cobbles and bridges

name: Almeirim (Brazil Amazon)
summary: Almeirim is an Amazon River cruise port and the northernmost municipality in Brazil's Para State. The town covers a total area of approx 73 km2 (28 mi2) and has a population of around 30,000.
description: Almeirim is an Amazon River cruise port and the northernmost municipality in Brazil's Para State. The town covers a total area of approx 73 km2 (28 mi2) and has a population of around 30,000. Almeirim is located approx 483 km (300 ml) up the Amazon River from the Atlantic ocean, and halfway between Santarem and Belem . The municipality encompasses a large part (95%) of the Maicuru Biological Reserve, covering a total area of approx 11518 km2 (4447 ml2). Serra do Areao Airport is in Monte Dourado district - approx 73 km (45 ml) away from the city. Among the largest ever cruise ships that have stopped in Almeirim Brazil is the Phoenix Reisen ship Albatros (on January 16, 2018) as part of an Around The World Cruise itinerary roundtrip from Hamburg Germany . The smaller itinerary segment (Jan 13-31, 20-days long) that included Almeirim started in Manaus and ended in Buenos Aires (Argentina) . Independent sightseeing with some planning. Almeirim is a small, remote Amazon River town rather than a conventional cruise destination. The central waterfront, historic buildings and main squares can be explored on foot, but rainforest and waterfall trips require pre-arranged transport, a local guide and considerably more time. Almeirim has a passenger river terminal on Avenida Beira Rio, close to the town center. However, expedition ships may use tenders or Zodiac boats instead of the local terminal, depending on the vessel, river level and operating conditions. Follow the ship's instructions for the landing point and final return time. If passengers land near the river terminal, Praça do Centenário is approximately 0.3 km (0.2 mi) away. Much of central Almeirim is walkable, although sidewalks can be uneven and shade is limited. Do not expect a large cruise terminal, organized taxi rank or frequent tourist transport.

things_to_do.name: Explore Central Almeirim
things_to_do.description: Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for an unhurried look at the riverfront and compact town center. The principal sights include Praça do Centenário, the Church of Our Lady of the Conception, Praça do Relógio and several early-20th-century civic buildings. The appeal is the everyday atmosphere of an isolated Amazonian community rather than major monuments.

things_to_do.name: Walk Along the Amazon Waterfront
things_to_do.description: The riverfront provides views of local passenger boats, cargo activity and the broad Amazon River. Conditions can change with seasonal flooding, so remain on established streets and paths. Avoid entering working areas or photographing people at close range without permission.

things_to_do.name: Experience Local Culture and Food
things_to_do.description: Small shops, markets or temporary fairs may offer regional fruit, fish dishes, snacks and handicrafts. Availability is irregular, and English may be limited. Carry small Brazilian-real notes because cards and foreign currency may not always be accepted.

things_to_do.name: Take a Ship-Organized Community or Nature Visit
things_to_do.description: If the cruise program includes a guided community visit, small-boat wildlife outing or forest activity, it will usually be more practical than arranging one after arrival. Local logistics are limited, and independent travelers should not assume that boats, guides or vehicles will be waiting at the landing place.

things_to_do.name: Easy Central Almeirim Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 1.5–2 km (0.9–1.2 mi) round trip Pure walking time: 25–35 minutes Recommended time: 1.5–2 hours with stops Difficulty: Easy, but heat, humidity and uneven surfaces can make the walk more tiring. Passenger landing or river terminal: Begin with views across the Amazon and observe the local river traffic. Avenida Beira Rio: Follow the central waterfront without entering restricted or working areas. Praça do Centenário: Walk inland to the town's principal public square, approximately 0.3 km (0.2 mi) from the river terminal. Church of Our Lady of the Conception: View the parish church and neighboring historic buildings. Interior access depends on whether the church is open. Historic center: Continue past older civic architecture, including the former municipal building and traditional streets around the center. Praça do Relógio: Pause at the clock square before returning toward the waterfront. Return to the landing: Retrace the central streets and allow extra time if the ship is operating tenders. Street signage may be limited, so save the landing location before starting. Avoid extending the walk into unfamiliar outskirts without a guide.
things_to_do.difficulty: Easy, but heat, humidity and uneven surfaces can make the walk more tiring

Almeria is a major Mediterranean port and city in Spain's Andalusia (autonomous region in southeastern Spain) with population around 200,000. Almeria is also a large ferry port serving the routes to Northern Africa (Morocco and Spanish Morocco). Almeria was founded because of the need for a better defense system for regional Arab towns. Abd-al-Rahman III (Cordoba's Emir between 912-29) founded the Citadel (Alcazaba), which gave this city its name: "the Watchtower" (Al-Mari'yah). In 2000, geologists found a cave in an abandoned silver mine (close to Almeria) filled with huge gypsum crystals. The cavity (measuring 1,8 x 1,7 m) is currently the biggest geode (spherical rock containing a hollow cavity lined with crystals) ever found. The cave's entrance has been blocked by 5 tons of rocks and is now under police protection in order to prevent looters from entering. It is also not accessible to tourists. According to existing geological models, this unique cave was formed around 6 million years ago, when the Mediterranean Sea evaporated and left layers of salt sediments. The city's economy is mostly based on agriculture, located mainly in the western part of the area. Numerous greenhouses produce tonnes of fruit and vegetables with over 70% of the production being exported to the rest of Europe. Puerto de Almeria (locode ESLEI) serves sea connections to Algeria, Morocco and Melilla, and also Mediterranean ship cruises. A major development project expanded the facility with new docks and Almeria became a container port with capacity to handle large-sized boxships . The Port also has a premium marina with moorings for yachts and pleasure boats. Regularly scheduled ferries connect Almeria with Algeria ( Oran , Ghazaouet) and Morocco ( Melilla , Nador). For 2018-H1 (first half), Port Almeria exported a total of 1,352804 million tons of solid bulk cargoes, the most exported of which are plaster, cement, and clinker (cement lumps). These cargoes go mainly to the UK and Ireland, and Africa - Morocco, Ivory Coast, Cameroon, Ghana. On November 23, 2020, the Spanish passenger shipping company BALEARIA carried out Port Almeria's first-ever LNG bunkering operation by supplying with LNG (liquefied natural gas) the cruiseferry Bahama Mama . Alofi is the capital city of the Pacific Ocean island nation Niue, situated within the Realm of New Zealand. Alofi has a population of 1,600 people (2011 census), and the distinction of being the 2nd smallest national capital city (first is Ngerulmud, Palau's capital) in terms of population. It consists of the 2 villages named Alofi North and Alofi South where the headquarters of the government are located. Alofi has a total area of 46.48 km2 (17.95 mi2). It is located at the central part of Alofi Bay on the island's west coast, near the only break in the coral reef which surrounds Niue. Alofi Bay stretches for 30% of the length of the island (about 7 km) from Makapu Point in the north to Halagigie Point in the south. It is also notable that the city of Alofi contains the largest toothbrush fence in the world. Niue was hit by the tropical storm Cyclone Heta in January 2004. Two people were killed. Heta did extensive damage to the entire island. Lots of the buildings of Alofi were destroyed, including the hospital. The buildings of the government were shifted to a less exposed site named Fonuakula, 3 km (1.9 mi) inland from the west coast, after the storm. The site is still within the boundaries of Alofi South village. Cruise ships to Niue Island dock (anchor) at Alofi - port town on the central-western coast. Smaller vessels are moored, while larger ships anchor near the port and their passengers are transported via the ship's tender boats. The following map of Niue Island shows all towns/villages, as well as the island's road infrastructure and the location of Niue International Airport (aka "Hanan International Airport") near Alofi. The airport currently serves only Air New Zealand flights to/from Auckland NZ . Flights are twice a week, leaving from Auckland on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and leaving from Niue Island on Tuesdays and Fridays. Alotau is the capital city of Milne Bay Province, located in the southeast of Papua New Guinea. Alotau (population around 16,000) lies on Milne Bay's northern shore. The city is located within the region in which the invading Japanese army suffered first land defeat during the Pacific War (1942), before the Kokoda Track battle. At the old battle site, a memorial park commemorates the event. In 1969, when shifted from Samarai, Alotau became a provincial capital. There is a road to Alotau from Ulumani which passes by the local Gurney Airport, which was named after squadron leader of the Royal Australian Air Force, Charles Raymond Gurney, who was killed in this area in 1942. Milne Bay is noted for its scuba diving and coral reef experiences. Alpena MI (port locode USALP ) is a Lake Huron cruise port and city in the USA's Michigan state (Alpena County ) with population around 10,000, ranking it Northern Michigan region's second-largest (after Traverse City ). Alpena County has total population around 30,000. The region's best-known attraction is Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary and Underwater Preserve which has 116 historically important shipwrecks - including wooden paddlewheelers and steel steamships. Most tourists come during the summer. Popular for recreational activities (biking and hiking) are also the Alpena to Hillman Trail (24 mi / 39 km, includes the abandoned Boyne City Railroad) and the North Eastern State Trail (Alpena to Cheboygan, 71 mi / 114 km, includes the abandoned Detroit and Mackinac Railroad/Turtle Line). Alpena MI's economy is based on tourism (including accommodation rentals and shopping) and large businesses like MidMichigan Health (non-profit, University of Michigan's healthcare division), Lafargeholcim Company (the world's largest cement plant, 1907-founded in Detroit as "Huron Portland Cement Company", annual capacity 2,4+ million MT/metric tonnes), Besser Company (concrete block machinery manufacturer), Decorative Panels International (drywall board manufacturer). In Rogers City (close to the north) is the world's largest limestone quarry. Alpena's historical landmarks include City Hall, County Courthouse, Daniel Carter Family Home, Monarch Mill, St Bernard Catholic Church, Congregational Church, Besser Museum and Planetarium, Great Lakes Maritime Heritage Center. In 2022, Viking Cruises USA (via the brand Viking Expeditions) starts a Great Lakes seasonal program. The ship deployment is for one-way itineraries (between homeports Toronto, Thunder Bay, Milwaukee) and includes regular visits to ports and destinations in Canada's Ontario state ( Thunder Bay , Toronto , Welland Canal, Niagara Falls, Point Pelee NP) and the USA's Minnesota-Michigan-Wisconsin states ( Detroit MI , Alpena MI, Mackinac Island MI in Lake Huron , Apostle Islands MI, Houghton MI , Traverse City MI , Milwaukee WI on Lake Michigan , Duluth MN ). All Viking Great Lakes cruises feature passing through Soo Locks at Sault Ste Marie (Lake Superior - Lake Huron transition). The 8-day voyages are themed "Niagara and the Great Lakes" (from Toronto to Milwaukee), "Undiscovered Great Lakes" (from Thunder Bay to Milwaukee) and "Great Lakes Explorer" (from Milwaukee to Thunder Bay).
