Alphonse Island (aka Alphonse Atoll) is a private island in Coralline Seychelles (Outer Islands) and part of the Alphonse Atoll group comprising 3 islands (Alphonse, St Francois, Bijoutier). The atoll is located approx 400 km (250 mi) southwest of Mahe Island (on which is Victoria - the country's capital city, principal port and primary cruise port), Alphonse Island is just 2 km (1 mi) north of St Francois Atoll (grouping two islands - Bijoutier and St Francois). Alphonse Island is the only one that is inhabited (population under 200), all of whom work for IDC (Islands Development Company Ltd). The island has a total area of 1,7 km2 (0,7 mi2), while the atoll group covers a marine area of approx 5,5km (3 mi) in diameter. The island is served by Alphonse Airport (crossing it diagonally) with regularly scheduled weekly domestic flights (by IDC) to Mahe's Seychelles International Airport. Air Seychelles operates charter flights to Mahe. St Francois Atoll (in the Alphonse Group) is separated from the Alphonse Group by Canal de Mort (deepwater sea channel). St Francois Atoll groups St Francois Island and Bijoutier Island, and both are currently uninhabited. The islands' combined land area is 0,5 km2 (0,2 mi2). St Francois Island has land area 0,47 km2 (0,18 mi2), coastline 10 km (6 mi), and is less than 30-min boat ride from Alphonse Island. St Francois is approx 9 km south of Bijoutier. Bijoutier Island has land area 0,03 km2 (0,01 mi2) and coastline 700 m. St Francois Atoll is a nesting habitat for hawksbill turtles and green turtles.

Alta (port locode NOALF) is a port city located in Alta Municipality (Finnmark County, Norway). It is is the administrative center of the municipality and it is situated on the southern end of Altafjorden, at the mouth of the Altaelva River. Several suburbs are found around the town. Rafsbotn lies to the east, Kafjord, Kvenvik, and Jiepmaluokta to the west, Ovre Alta and Tverrelvdalen to the south. The famous Alta rock carvings lie just to the west of the city. Alta is considered the world's northernmost city with a population that surpasses 10,000 inhabitants. It was established in 2000 when Elvebakken, Bossekop, and Alta villages were joined together and declared a town by the municipality council. The town has a population around 14,000 (density 1577 people per km2 / 4080 per mi2). Alta has 3 churches: the historic Alta Church (Bossekop), the relatively new Elvebakken Church (Elvebakken), and the Northern Lights Cathedral (new "main" church for the municipality, completed in 2013). Alta is an educational center in Finnmark county. The Finnmark University College and the local primary and secondary schools are based in Alta. Alta District Court serves the municipalities of Alta and Loppa. Alta is also a center of transportation in Finnmark county. It has port facilities along Altafjorden, just alongside Alta Airport (Elvebakken). The airport provides direct flights to Oslo . European route E06 highway runs through the town. Main industries in Alta include several wood mills and sawmills; dairy, horticulture trade, a concrete product factory, and maritime services. Alton IL (port locode USALT ) is a Mississippi River cruise port and town in Illinois USA (Madison County), located approx 15 mi (24 km) north of St Louis MO (Missouri) . The town has a population of around 28,000 and is a part of the Greater St Louis metro area. Cruise ships to Alton IL dock near Alton Marina (adjacent to Clark Bridge). As cruise port, Alton is included in the schedule of AQSC (American Queen Voyages/Steamboat Company) and visited by the AQSC's riverboats American Queen and American Duchess . The closest cruise port is Hannibal MO . The town's architecture is dominated by traditional Victorian-style houses. The downtown (and the commercial district) is located at the top of a hill. The current-day economy is based on river shipping (mainly cargo barges), manufacturing (Laclede Steel, Cope Plastics, Hanley Industries), agriculture, and tourism. Due to its location at the river, Alton IL suffered severe damages during the Great Flood of 1993 when Mississippi and Missouri rivers flooded an area sized ~320,000 mi2 (~830,000 km2) and for 3 weeks the town remained completely cut off. The flood was among the USA's most devastating and the damages were estimated at ~USD 15 billion (~26 billion in 2018-USD). Clark Bridge (1994-opened, designed by Hanson Engineers Springfield IL) over Mississippi River interlinks Alton IL and West Alton MO. Clark Bridge is cable-stayed and four-lane (plus 2 bike lanes) and carrying the north-south US highway Route 67 (two lanes in each direction). Alton's tourism industry started to develop in the early-20th century. The city's location and historical heritage (American Civil War) make it a popular destination for touring, gambling weddings-honeymoons, gourmet dining, nightlife. Best-known attractions include Argosy Casino, Alton Marina, premium golf courses, high-rated B&B inns, and guest houses. A designated bike path extends from north of downtown along the river and below the scenic limestone bluffs. Pere Marquette State Park (Jersey County, near Grafton IL, at the confluence of Mississippi-Illinois rivers) is popular for hiking and horse riding.

Amalfi is a port city in Italy's Campania region (Salerno province) with population around 5,000. The port (locode ITAMA) is on Salerno Gulf. The town is at the Monte Cerreto's foot (1315 m / 4314 ft) and surrounded by coastal scenery and dramatic cliffs. Between 958-1137, Amalfi was the capital of the maritime Republic of Amalfi (aka Duchy of Amalfi). In the 1920s-1930s, Amalfi was a popular holiday destination for the upper class and aristocracy in Britain. Amalfi is the main town of the coast on which it is situated, named Costiera Amalfitana (Amalfi Coast). Today it is an important tourist destination together with other cities on the same coast, such as Ravello, Positano , and others. Amalfi is included in UNESCO World Heritage Sites. A patron saint of the city is Saint Andrew, the Apostle, whose relics are kept at Amalfi Cathedral (Cattedrale di Sant'Andrea/Duomo di Amalfi). Amalfi is a compact and rewarding port call. Cruise ships normally anchor offshore and bring passengers ashore by tender, usually close to the ferry pier and town center. The cathedral, historic lanes, waterfront and beach are all within a short walk. Independent sightseeing: Easy independently for Amalfi itself. Ravello and neighboring coastal towns are also possible with planning, but traffic, crowded buses, seasonal ferry schedules and tender operations require extra time.
getting_from_port: Tender landing: Passengers normally land at or near Amalfi’s central waterfront. The exact landing arrangement can vary by ship and local conditions. Town center: Piazza Duomo is approximately 300 m (0.2 mi) inland, reached in about five minutes on foot. Walking: No shuttle is normally needed for central Amalfi. Most lanes are pedestrianized, but routes away from the waterfront quickly encounter steps and slopes. Local transport: Public buses and taxis leave from the waterfront area. Seasonal ferries connect Amalfi with other coastal towns, subject to weather and operating schedules. Tender conditions: Wind or rough seas can delay tendering. Confirm the final return tender time before leaving the landing area.

things_to_do.name: Explore Amalfi on Foot
things_to_do.description: Recommended time: 2–3 hours. This is the simplest independent option and works well even during a relatively short call. Walk from the waterfront to Piazza Duomo and visit the Cathedral of Saint Andrew, its monumental staircase and the adjoining cloister and museum complex. Continue along Via Lorenzo d’Amalfi, then follow the narrow main valley past shops, small squares, fountains and historic buildings.

things_to_do.name: Visit the Paper Museum and Valley of the Mills
things_to_do.description: Recommended time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: Moderate, with a gradual uphill walk. The Paper Museum occupies a historic mill approximately 800 m (0.5 mi) inland from the waterfront. Continue beyond it into the quieter upper valley to see old mill structures, streams and steep lemon-growing terraces. This shorter valley walk provides some of the atmosphere of the Valle delle Ferriere without committing to a long hike.
things_to_do.difficulty: Moderate, with a gradual uphill walk

things_to_do.name: Combine Amalfi with Ravello
things_to_do.description: Recommended time: 4–5 hours. Independent with planning or transport. Ravello lies about 7 km (4.3 mi) from Amalfi by road, high above the coast. Public buses generally take around 25–35 minutes when traffic is flowing, while a taxi or locally operated shuttle may be more predictable. In Ravello, focus on the compact center and one major villa garden, such as Villa Rufolo or Villa Cimbrone. Allow for queues and delays on the winding road. During busy periods, buses can be crowded, so a ship excursion, prearranged transfer or taxi may be preferable when the port call is short.

things_to_do.name: See Another Coastal Town by Ferry
things_to_do.description: Recommended time: At least 4–5 hours. Independent with careful planning. When seasonal ferry services are operating, traveling by sea is usually more comfortable and predictable than using the congested coastal road. Atrani, Minori, Maiori or Positano may be possible depending on the day’s timetable. Choose one destination rather than attempting several towns. Check departures and return sailings after arriving ashore. Ferries can be changed or cancelled because of sea conditions, so do not rely on the final available service back to Amalfi.

things_to_do.name: Relax at the Waterfront
things_to_do.description: Recommended time: 1–3 hours. Marina Grande beach is beside the harbor and is the most convenient place for swimming. Much of it is operated by beach clubs, with a smaller public section. The beach is pebbly, so water shoes can be useful.

things_to_do.name: Easy Amalfi Highlights Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: About 2 km (1.2 mi) round trip Pure walking time: 30–40 minutes Recommended total time: 2–3 hours Difficulty: Easy to moderate; mostly compact streets, with a substantial staircase at the cathedral. Tender landing and waterfront: Begin beside the harbor and walk toward the center. Piazza Duomo: Enter Amalfi’s main square, approximately five minutes from the waterfront. Cathedral of Saint Andrew: Climb the broad steps and allow time for the cathedral complex. Via Lorenzo d’Amalfi: Follow the town’s pedestrian spine past shops, cafés and narrow side lanes. Paper Museum: Continue gradually uphill through the valley to the historic mill. Return through the old lanes: Retrace the main route or explore parallel alleys where accessible. Waterfront: Finish near the tender pier, beach and ferry terminal.

things_to_do.name: Amalfi and Atrani Walk
things_to_do.description: Distance: About 3 km (1.9 mi) round trip Pure walking time: 50–70 minutes Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours Difficulty: Moderate, with steps, inclines and uneven lanes. Amalfi waterfront: Walk through Piazza Duomo and the eastern side of the old town. Upper pedestrian lanes: Follow the signed passages and stairways toward Atrani. Atrani: Descend into the small central square and explore the lanes around the church and beach. Return to Amalfi: Retrace the pedestrian route rather than walking through road tunnels without a proper pedestrian path. Atrani is only about 1 km (0.6 mi) from central Amalfi, but the stepped route is more demanding than the short distance suggests.
things_to_do.difficulty: Moderate, with steps, inclines and uneven lanes

things_to_do.name: Valle delle Ferriere
things_to_do.description: The complete valley experience requires several hours and involves rough paths, elevation changes and potentially confusing junctions. A common route begins above Amalfi near Pontone and descends for approximately 6 km (3.7 mi), taking around 3–4 hours before transport and stops. Organized excursion or experienced independent planning recommended. Wear proper walking shoes, carry water and confirm whether access to protected sections requires advance arrangements or a guide. This hike is unsuitable for a short or uncertain tender call.

things_to_do.name: Private Coastal Drive or Boat Trip
things_to_do.description: A prearranged vehicle can combine Amalfi with Ravello and viewpoints along the coast. A local boat trip offers coastal scenery without road traffic, but weather and sea conditions determine whether it operates. For either option, use a reputable operator and agree on a return time that leaves a substantial margin before the final tender.

things_to_do.name: Pompeii or the Path of the Gods
things_to_do.description: Both require considerable travel or hiking time. They are best attempted on a long port call through a ship excursion or carefully organized transfer. They leave little flexibility if coastal traffic, transport connections or tendering are delayed.

Amami Oshima Island is one of Japan's Satsunan Islands (Kagoshima Prefecture). Being the largest within the Amami archipelago, the island covers a total area of approx 712 km2 (275 mi2) and has a population of around 73,000. Administratively, the island is divided into Amami city, the towns of Tatsugo, Setouchi, and the villages Yamato and Uken. Much of the island is within Amami Gunto Quasi-National Park. Amami Oshima is Japan's 7th largest island in the Japanese archipelago, excluding the disputed Kuril Islands. It is approx 380 km (210 mi) south of the southern tip of Kyushu Island and approx 250 km (130 mi) north of Okinawa. The island's highest elevation point (Mount Yuwanda) is 605 m (1985 ft) above sea level. The coast is surrounded by a coral reef. The Pacific Ocean is on the east and the East China Sea - on the west. The climate is humid subtropical, with mild winters and very warm summers. The rainy season is May through September. The island is subject to repeated typhoons. The island's economy is based mainly on agriculture (rice, sweet potatoes, sugarcane), commercial fishing, the distillation of shochu (an alcoholic beverage with 45% alcohol by volume), and seasonal tourism. The favorable climate allows for 2 rice crops per year. Traditional crafts include hand-made silk. Amami City's Port Naze is a major regional ferry port. The island is also served by Amami Airport (on the northern end) linking it via domestic flights with Tokyo , Naha , Fukuoka , Kagoshima and Osaka , and via short flights to other Amami islands. Since March 2018, Amami-Oshima is connected to the Yakushima islands via a weekly cruise ferry service. The charter flight service between the islands was started in February 2018. Amami-Oshima tourism was also boosted by the introduction of new routes connecting sightseeing sites in Kagoshima Prefecture. Until 2018, there were no ferries or flights directly linking the islands. The ferry service's 1-year trial started on March 4, 2018. The regularly scheduled service is offered once every 4 days. It links Naha with Kagoshima via Port Naze (Amami-Oshima Island). The cruise ferry also visits Port Miyanoura ( Yakushima Island ) if at least 20 passengers make reservations. Cruise ships to Amami Oshima Island dock (anchor) at Amami (Port Naze) - a port town located on the northern coast. Independent with some planning or transport. Central Naze is close enough for an easy independent visit, but Amami Oshima’s mangroves, beaches and protected forests are spread across a large island. Taxis, a pre-arranged driver or an organized excursion are more practical than relying on infrequent buses for the main nature sights. Ships generally call at Naze Port on the northwestern side of Amami Oshima. The Nagahama area has a dedicated cruise berth, although the exact arrival arrangement can depend on the ship and local operations. Check the onboard notice to confirm whether your sailing will dock or use tenders.
terminal_notes: The Nagahama area has a dedicated cruise berth, although the exact arrival arrangement can depend on the ship and local operations.
tender_evidence: Check the onboard notice to confirm whether your sailing will dock or use tenders.

things_to_do.name: Mangrove Canoeing
things_to_do.description: The mangrove forest at Kuroshio no Mori Mangrove Park is one of the island’s signature experiences. It is approximately 30–40 minutes by road from central Naze, with organized canoe sessions generally lasting about one hour. Allow approximately 3–4 hours for transfers, check-in and paddling. A pre-booked excursion or private transfer is preferable because canoe departures are scheduled and public buses may not fit the ship’s timetable. Conditions in the channels vary with the tide.

things_to_do.name: Naze Town and Amami Culture
things_to_do.description: For a flexible day without a long transfer, explore Naze independently. The Amami City Amami Museum in Nagahama introduces the island’s natural environment, history and traditional life. Continue into the commercial center for local food, shops and examples of Oshima Tsumugi silk textiles. This option needs approximately 2–3 hours and is the safest choice for a short call, uncertain weather or passengers who prefer to remain close to the ship.

things_to_do.name: Ohama Seaside Park
things_to_do.description: Ohama Seaside Park combines a coral-sand beach, coastal views, a promenade and the Amami Ocean Exhibition Hall. It is approximately 15–20 minutes by taxi from central Naze. Allow 2–3 hours including transport. Swimming should depend on weather, sea conditions and any local warnings; the beach is also worthwhile simply for a coastal walk. Arrange the return taxi rather than assuming one will be waiting.

things_to_do.name: Kinsakubaru Forest
things_to_do.description: Kinsakubaru protects subtropical old-growth forest and endemic wildlife. Entry is permitted only with a certified eco-tour guide, reservations are required, and vehicle numbers are controlled. The forest route is approximately 2 km (1.2 mi), generally taking 1.5–2 hours on foot. Organized excursion recommended. Access involves narrow mountain roads, and there is no reliable mobile-phone signal in parts of the area. Allow at least half a day including transfers.

things_to_do.name: Island Highlights by Car
things_to_do.description: A private driver or organized tour can combine one principal nature experience with a beach, viewpoint or textile-related stop. Avoid attempting both the far north and far south during an ordinary port call: the island is long, roads are often winding, and transfers take longer than distances may suggest.

things_to_do.name: Easy Town and Culture Route
things_to_do.description: Route: Nagahama cruise berth – Amami City Amami Museum – Nagahama waterfront – central shopping streets – Yanigawa entertainment district – return to the port. Begin at the passenger exit and walk through Nagahama to the Amami City Amami Museum. Allow time for the exhibits if the museum is open during the call. Continue toward central Naze and its covered and open-air shopping streets. Walk through the Yanigawa area, known locally for its compact lanes of restaurants and small bars. Stop for an Amami-style meal or browse for local silk goods before retracing the route to the ship. The complete circuit is approximately 4 km (2.5 mi), with about 50–60 minutes of pure walking. Allow 2–3 hours with museum, shopping and refreshment stops. The route is mostly flat and easy, although summer heat, humidity and heavy rain can make it tiring.

name: Amarapura (Myanmar)
summary: Amarapura is the former capital of Myanmar. Now it is a township of Mandalay , bounded by Chanmyathazi township in the north, Irrawaddy river in the west, and the ancient capital site of Ava in the south.
description: Amarapura is the former capital of Myanmar. Now it is a township of Mandalay , bounded by Chanmyathazi township in the north, Irrawaddy river in the west, and the ancient capital site of Ava in the south. Amarapura was twice the capital of Myanmar during the Konbaung period (1783–1821, 1842–1859) before in 1859 finally being displaced by Mandalay 11 km north. It is historically referred to as Southern City (Taungmyo) in relation to Mandalay. Today, Amarapura is part of Mandalay, which is the result of urban sprawl. It is famous for its traditional cotton and silk weaving, and bronze casting. Amarapura is also a popular day-trip tourist destination from Mandalay. Sights of interest in Amarapura include the Pahtodawgyi (stupa built in 1816 by King Bodawpaya outside the city walls), Bagaya Monastery (wooden monastery that was founded by King Mindon), Kyauktawgyi Pagoda (stupa built in 1847 by King Pagan at the farther end of U Bein bridge), U Bein Bridge (1.2 km wooden footbridge which is the world's longest teak bridge, built by mayor U Bein salvaging unwanted teak columns from Amarapura's old palace during a move to Mandalay), Amarapura Palace ruins (tombs of King Bodawpaya, King Bagyidaw, and part of old moat), Chinese Temple (built 1838 during the reign of King Tharrawaddy), Maha Gandhayon Monastery (modern monastery complex well known throughout the country), Yadanabon University (major liberal arts university). Organized excursion recommended. Amarapura is an excursion-oriented river-cruise stop rather than a conventional port with a fixed passenger terminal. Landing points and arrangements can vary with the vessel, river level and itinerary. The main sights are spread out, local transport is not standardized, and current security conditions in Myanmar require particular caution. River ships normally use a simple landing rather than a purpose-built cruise terminal. Passengers should follow the cruise operator’s instructions because the landing may not be within practical walking distance of U Bein Bridge or other attractions. Prearranged vehicles are the most reliable way to explore. Do not assume that taxis, public transport, signage or English-speaking drivers will be available at the landing. Confirm the meeting point and return time before leaving the ship.
terminal_notes: Amarapura is an excursion-oriented river-cruise stop rather than a conventional port with a fixed passenger terminal. River ships normally use a simple landing rather than a purpose-built cruise terminal.

things_to_do.name: U Bein Bridge and Taungthaman Lake
things_to_do.description: Amarapura’s principal attraction is the teak U Bein Bridge, extending approximately 1.2 km (0.7 mi) across Taungthaman Lake. Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for a partial or complete walk, photographs and time beside the lake. The bridge can be narrow, uneven and exposed to strong sun. Some sections have limited edge protection, so it is unsuitable for visitors who are unsteady on their feet. Conditions around the lake change seasonally with the water level.

things_to_do.name: Mahagandayon Monastery
things_to_do.description: This large monastic community is commonly combined with U Bein Bridge. Visit quietly, dress conservatively and avoid obstructing monks or daily routines. Photography may be inappropriate in some situations, so follow local guidance. A guided visit is preferable because access and visitor arrangements can change.

things_to_do.name: Traditional Silk Weaving
things_to_do.description: Amarapura is associated with traditional silk and cotton weaving. Some guided visits include a working workshop where passengers can see looms in use. This is best arranged through the cruise operator or a local guide rather than attempted independently from the river landing.

things_to_do.name: Mandalay Highlights
things_to_do.description: Mandalay lies roughly 11 km (6.8 mi) north of the U Bein Bridge area. With a sufficiently long call, an excursion may combine Amarapura with selected Mandalay sights such as Mahamuni Buddha Temple, Shwenandaw Monastery or Kuthodaw Pagoda. Traffic can make travel times unpredictable, so a tightly packed independent itinerary is not advisable.

things_to_do.name: Inwa and Sagaing
things_to_do.description: Inwa’s former royal sites and the monasteries of Sagaing can form a broader full-day excursion with Amarapura. The route involves road travel and, depending on the itinerary, local boats or additional transfers. Choose this option only when the ship provides a long port call and coordinated transport.

things_to_do.name: Bridge and Lakeside Route
things_to_do.description: Begin at the main bridge approach beside Taungthaman Lake. Walk onto U Bein Bridge, stopping only where there is enough space for others to pass. Continue across the lake for changing views of the bridge, fishing boats and shoreline. At the opposite bank, visit the exterior and grounds of Kyauktawgyi Pagoda if accessible. Return across the bridge to the original meeting point. Distance: approximately 2.5–3 km (1.6–1.9 mi) round trip, depending on detours. Pure walking time: about 45–60 minutes. Allow 1.5–2 hours with stops. Difficulty: moderate because of uneven timber, narrow sections, heat and limited shade. Wear secure footwear and carry water. Visitors uncomfortable with the full crossing can walk partway and return by the same route.
things_to_do.difficulty: moderate because of uneven timber, narrow sections, heat and limited shade

summary: Port Amarna cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link. Amarna (Akhetaton) is a Nile River cruise port and an Ancient Egyptian city (in Upper Egypt's Minya Governorate) where are the ruins of Egypt's capital established in 1346 BC by the 18th Dynasty Pharaoh Akhenaten. The city was built by Akhenaten but was abandoned just after 14 years (in 1332 BC) after the king's death. Amarna is on Nile's east bank and located approx 60 km (36 mi) south Al-Minya , approx 310 km (190 mi) south of Cairo and approx 400 km (250 mi) north of Luxor . The closest to Amarna modern city is Deir Mawas - approx 7 km to the west (directly across the river). Amarna was intended as a capital dedicated to new worship - to Aten (Aton) - symbolized with the Sun Disc (an aspect of god Ra). Although the city was completed in 1341 BC, it started to function as capital in 1343 BC. Most buildings were made using mud-bricks, while only the most important ones were stone-faced. As cruise port, Amarna is included in the regular schedule of the Movenpick Hotels and Resorts owned riverboat (hotel ship) Movenpick Darakum . The ship operates on 10-day and 14-day cruise tours between homeports Aswan and Luxor, with included domestic flights from or to Cairo. The next table shows the 10-day itinerary as a ports sequence. Prices start from ~USD 2500 per person (double occupancy cabin rates). Amarna is a specialist archaeological stop rather than a conventional port town. The remains of Akhenaten’s capital extend across a large desert site on the Nile’s east bank, and the principal monuments are too widely separated to explore on foot. Organized excursion recommended. Cruise visitors normally need a vehicle, site admission arrangements and an Egyptologist or knowledgeable guide. Independent sightseeing is possible only with transport arranged in advance. Nile vessels may use different local mooring or landing points, so passengers should follow the arrangements provided on board. The Amarna Visitor Centre is beside the Nile in El-Till, while the archaeological remains, ticket office and tombs are spread across the desert farther inland. There is no conventional cruise terminal or dependable tourist transport network. Do not plan to find a taxi after disembarking. A cruise excursion or pre-arranged car with a driver is the practical way to visit the site, and the vehicle should remain with you throughout the tour.
terminal_notes: There is no conventional cruise terminal or dependable tourist transport network.

things_to_do.name: Guided Highlights of Ancient Amarna
things_to_do.description: Allow about 3–5 hours for a useful introduction, depending on the ship’s schedule and which monuments are open. A typical vehicle-based visit may combine the North Palace, Small Aten Temple area, North Tombs and one or more viewpoints across the ancient city. The surviving remains are less monumental than those at Luxor, but a guide helps explain the ground plans, reliefs and unusual scenes from the reign of Akhenaten and Nefertiti. This is the best option for most cruise passengers.

things_to_do.name: North Tombs
things_to_do.description: The rock-cut tombs of Amarna’s officials preserve reliefs showing the royal family, Aten worship and buildings from the ancient city. Access involves high flights of stone steps, rough surfaces and additional walking along the cliff. Allow about 1–1.5 hours at the tomb area. This visit is unsuitable for passengers with significant mobility limitations. Tomb access can depend on the availability of guardians and local site arrangements.

things_to_do.name: Royal Tomb and Central City
things_to_do.description: On a longer call, a guided circuit may add the Royal Tomb and the remains of the ceremonial center. The Royal Tomb requires a descent by stairs and a sloping passage, while the Central City is primarily an archaeological landscape of foundations and reconstructed outlines. These sites add context but require more driving and time. They should be included only when the ship’s excursion schedule provides a comfortable return margin.

things_to_do.name: Amarna Visitor Centre
things_to_do.description: The visitor center in El-Till provides a useful introduction through Arabic- and English-language panels, models and a full-size reconstruction of an official’s house. It is the easiest part of Amarna for passengers with limited time or mobility, although the reconstructed house itself is not wheelchair accessible. A focused visit takes approximately 45–60 minutes. Confirm that it is included and open during the ship’s call rather than attempting to reach it independently from an unspecified landing point.

name: Amasra-Bartin (Turkey)
summary: Amasra is a Black Sea port town and the cruise port to Bartın City, both part of Turkey's Bartın Province. Amasra has population around 7,000, while Bartın (Province's capital) has population around 60,000. The road distance between Asra and Bartin is approx 13 km (8 mi) with tourist travel options buses and taxis.
description: Amasra is a Black Sea port town and the cruise port to Bartın City, both part of Turkey's Bartın Province. Amasra has population around 7,000, while Bartın (Province's capital) has population around 60,000. The road distance between Asra and Bartin is approx 13 km (8 mi) with tourist travel options buses and taxis. As cruise port, Bartin-Amasra is visited mainly by top-luxury ships and superyachts. Next table shows the "12-Night Black Sea Odyssey Cruise" itinerary scheduled for 2022 by the French company and premium travel brand Ponant for its ship Le Bougainville . Early booking prices started from USD 10500 per person with double occupancy. Amasra is also visited by the cruise ship Astoria Grande/fka AIDAcara arriving from homeport Sochi Russia (via Istanbul ) and also visiting Sinop . In 2022, Astoria Grande's schedule included 5x visits to Amasra (Sept 14 & 28, Oct 5, 12 & 19) with port stay between 8 am - 6 pm. Port Bartin (locode TRBTN) is on the Black Sea while the city is located inland (on Bartın River/navigable waterway) which allows access to the city directly from the Black Sea (approx 14 km / 9 mi sailing upstream) via smaller-sized ships, superyachts and boats. The settlement (as Parthenios/Parthenia) was established as an Ancient Greek colony, and later became part of the Imperium Romanum/Roman Empire, the Byzantium/Eastern Roman Empire and in the late-14th-century (1392) part of the Ottoman Empire (1299-1923). Port Amasra (locode TRAMA) was also founded by the Greeks under the name Amastris, and is mentioned in Homer's Iliad (aka Song of Ilion) together with three other Ionian colonies (Cromna, Sesamus, Cytorus). Amasra is popular for its Archaeological Museum (located on the waterfront) which has ruins both on land and underwater. Other tourist attractions include Amasra Castle (built by the Romans, fortified by the Byzantines and the Genoese), Fatih Mosque (9th-century Byzantine church), the Kuskayası Monument (akak Bird's Rock Road Monument/built by the Roman Governor Gaius Julius Aquila during the reign of Emperor Tiberius Claudius). In 2018 started the TL 78 million (USD 4,3m) project for building the new Amasra cruise port. In August 2022, the project was ~90% completed. Amasra is a compact Black Sea town where the principal sights, castle lanes, harbours and beaches fit comfortably into a half-day visit. Sightseeing is easy independently , although the historic quarters include slopes, steps and uneven paving.
getting_from_port: Most current cruise calls berth at Amasra Passenger Port on the eastern side of Büyük Liman. After completing port formalities, passengers can normally walk into the centre; the waterfront and first shops are roughly 1 km (0.6 mi) away, or about 10–20 minutes on foot. Some smaller-ship itineraries may use a different landing arrangement or identify the call as Amasra/Bartın, so confirm the actual arrival point and any shuttle information onboard. A vehicle is unnecessary for central Amasra but essential for Safranbolu and other regional excursions.

things_to_do.name: Amasra Castle and Boztepe
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours to explore the inhabited castle district, its surviving gates and walls, Kemere Bridge and the lanes of Boztepe. The elevated sections provide the best views across the two harbours. This is practical independently, but expect inclines, steps and irregular stone surfaces.

things_to_do.name: Harbours, Museum and Local Market
things_to_do.description: For a gentler visit, follow the Büyük Liman waterfront into town, browse the wooden crafts and souvenirs in Çekiciler Bazaar, and continue toward Amasra Museum and Küçük Liman. Allow around 2 hours, longer if visiting the museum or stopping for lunch. Check the museum’s opening status locally before relying on a visit.

things_to_do.name: Beach or Waterfront Lunch
things_to_do.description: Büyük Liman and Küçük Liman beaches are both within the central sightseeing area. A short beach stop can therefore be combined with the castle walk without arranging transport. Swimming conditions depend on Black Sea weather, and facilities may be limited outside the summer season. Waterfront restaurants are convenient for local fish and Amasra salad, but leave extra time when several tour groups are ashore.

things_to_do.name: Safranbolu
things_to_do.description: The UNESCO-listed Ottoman town of Safranbolu is approximately 95–100 km (59.0–62.1 mi) inland, normally around 1.5 hours each way by road. Its preserved houses, market lanes and historic public buildings make it the main full-day excursion from Amasra. An organized excursion or prearranged private vehicle is recommended. Ordinary public transport involves too much uncertainty for a cruise call. The round trip consumes at least 3 hours before sightseeing, so Safranbolu suits a long port stay rather than a short call.

things_to_do.name: Harbours and Castle Circuit
things_to_do.description: Distance: approximately 3.5 km (2.2 mi). Pure walking time: about 60–75 minutes. Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours. Difficulty: moderate, with slopes, stairs and uneven paving. Passenger-port exit: Follow the harbour road toward central Amasra. Büyük Liman: Walk beside the main bay and beach toward the town centre. Çekiciler Bazaar: Browse the compact market area known for locally made wooden items and souvenirs. Castle lanes: Enter the old quarter and follow the narrow streets through the surviving fortifications. Kemere Bridge: Cross the historic stone bridge linking the mainland castle section with Boztepe. Boztepe: Continue uphill through the residential lanes for coastal and harbour views. Küçük Liman: Descend toward the smaller harbour, beach and Amasra Museum area. Return: Walk through the modern centre and along Büyük Liman to the passenger port. The circuit can be shortened by omitting the higher Boztepe lanes. Passengers with limited mobility may prefer the relatively level waterfront, bazaar and museum area; the castle itself is less accessible.
things_to_do.difficulty: moderate, with slopes, stairs and uneven paving

Pulau Ambon Island is one of Indonesia's Maluku Islands. It has total area approx 775 km2 (299 mi2) and population around 450,000. Ambon is located off Seram island's southwest coast and on the north side of the Banda Sea. Ambon Island is mountainous, fertile and well-watered. Its main port and largest town is Ambon, which is also the capital of Maluku Tengah and Maluku province. Island's highest elevation points are Wawani (1100 m / 3600 ft) and Salahutu (1225 m / 4019 ft), both featuring hot springs as these mountains are actually volcanoes. Ambon Island's economy is based on agriculture, with main crops cassava and sago, also sugarcane, coffee, cocoa, breadfruit, cotton, pepper. Fishing and hunting supplement the local food. Copra (dried coconut) is also exported. Amboina wood (obtained from angsana trees) is highly valued and used for ornamental woodwork. Pulau Ambon's economy was boosted by Ciputra Group's investment in a satellite city (Citraland Bay View City) in Lateri (Kotamadya Ambon, Maluku). Ambon City Center (an international-standard shopping mall) was opened in 2012. Ambon has its own airport, private and state universities. Cruise ships to Pulau Ambon Island dock at Ambon - port city on the southern coast. Independent with some planning or transport. Ships generally use the port facilities beside central Ambon, although the assigned berth and whether tendering is required can vary. If passengers leave through Yos Sudarso Port, the commercial center is close enough for a short independent walk. Beaches, the war cemetery, museums and coastal scenery require a taxi, private driver or organized excursion.
getting_from_port: Ambon has several working port areas around its deep bay. Confirm the landing point and all-aboard arrangements in the ship's daily information rather than relying on the map marker. From Yos Sudarso Port: Central streets, markets and several landmarks are normally within walking distance of the passenger exit. Taxis and private vehicles: These are the most practical choice beyond downtown. Agree on the destination, total fare and return arrangements before leaving. Local minibuses: Angkot services cover the city and island, but routes are not designed for visitors and may involve changes. They are best avoided when time ashore is limited. Traffic: Ambon's roads can be congested, particularly through the center and around the bay. Allow additional time on the return journey.
terminal_notes: Ships generally use the port facilities beside central Ambon, although the assigned berth and whether tendering is required can vary.
tender_evidence: Ships generally use the port facilities beside central Ambon, although the assigned berth and whether tendering is required can vary.

things_to_do.name: Explore Central Ambon on Foot
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours for a compact introduction to local city life. The main points of interest include Al-Fatah Mosque, the busy commercial streets, Pattimura Park, the World Peace Gong and nearby churches. The experience is more about markets, street activity and modern Ambon than major monumental sights. This is the easiest independent option when the ship docks near the center. Pavements can be uneven or obstructed, road crossings require care, and the tropical heat makes the walk more tiring than its length suggests.

things_to_do.name: Combine Ambon War Cemetery with City Sights
things_to_do.description: Ambon War Cemetery is about 5 km (3.1 mi) northeast of central Ambon on the road toward Galala. The landscaped cemetery and memorial commemorate Allied personnel who died during the Second World War and in captivity. Allow roughly 2.5–3.5 hours for the cemetery, World Peace Gong and a short city circuit by taxi or private vehicle. This is practical independently if return transport is arranged; visitors with a particular interest in wartime history may prefer a guide.

things_to_do.name: Visit Museum Siwalima and the Southern Coast
things_to_do.description: Museum Siwalima is approximately 5 km (3.1 mi) from central Ambon and presents Maluku's regional culture and maritime heritage. Its location outside the walkable center makes a taxi necessary. Verify that the museum is open on the day of the call, as operating days and hours can change. With 4–5 hours, combine the museum with a scenic drive toward Namalatu or Pintu Kota. Pintu Kota is known for its natural sea arch and rocky shoreline and is about a 45-minute drive from downtown under favorable conditions. It is primarily a scenery and photography stop rather than a conventional sandy swimming beach.

things_to_do.name: Relax at Natsepa Beach
things_to_do.description: Natsepa Beach is around 18 km (11.2 mi) east of central Ambon, normally about 30–45 minutes each way depending on traffic. It has a gently sloping beach, local food stalls and views across Baguala Bay. Trying the local fruit-and-peanut dish known as rujak Natsepa is part of the visit. Allow at least 4 hours including transport. A prearranged driver, taxi waiting for the return or organized beach transfer is preferable. Check sea conditions locally before swimming and do not leave valuables unattended.

things_to_do.name: Take an Island Highlights Excursion
things_to_do.description: A guided or private-vehicle circuit is the most efficient option for combining several dispersed sights. A realistic route may include Ambon War Cemetery, a bay viewpoint, a village stop and either Natsepa Beach or the southern coastal scenery. Trying to include both distant sides of the island can result in too much time in traffic. Organized excursion recommended for passengers who want multiple island sights, reliable transport and local interpretation within one call.

things_to_do.name: Easy to Moderate City Route
things_to_do.description: Route: Yos Sudarso Port passenger exit – Al-Fatah Mosque area – central market and shopping streets – World Peace Gong – Pattimura Park – Maranatha Church area – return to the port. Approximate distance: 3 km (1.9 mi), depending on the port gate and chosen streets. Pure walking time: About 45–60 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–2.5 hours with stops. Difficulty: Easy in distance but moderate in heat; mostly urban and relatively level. Conditions: Expect busy traffic, irregular pavements, limited shade in places and frequent road crossings. Religious buildings should be viewed quietly and entered only when visitors are welcome. Wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees. Retrace the route or take a short taxi back if conditions are too hot, leaving ample time to clear the port entrance.
things_to_do.difficulty: Easy in distance but moderate in heat

region: Australia - New Zealand - Pacific Ocean Islands
summary: Port Ambrym Island Vanuatu cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link.
description: Port Ambrym Island Vanuatu cruise ship schedule shows timetable calendars of all arrival and departure dates by month. The port's schedule lists all ships (in links) with cruises going to or leaving from Ambrym Island Vanuatu. To see the full itineraries (ports of call dates and arrival / departure times) and their lowest rates – just follow the corresponding ship-link. Ambrym Island (port locode VUVLI) is in Vanuatu's Malampa Province. The island covers a total area of approx 678 km2 (262 mi2), ranking it Vanuatu's 5th largest. Its population (around 7,000) live mainly off coconut plantations in the 3 corners of the isle. Ambrym's volcanic activity includes lava lakes in 2 craters close to the summit. The island was discovered in 1774 by James Cook (1728-1779 / Royal Navy Captain, explorer, cartographer). Located close to the center of Vanuatu archipelago, Ambrym is roughly triangular in shape, with a width of approx 50 km (31 mi). Island's summit is dominated by a desert-like caldera covering an area of 100 km2 (39 mi2). Except for the human settlements, the rest of the island is covered by jungle. The caldera measures 12x8 km (7,5x5 mi) and has 2 active volcanic cones (Marum and Benbow). Several times per century, the Ambrym volcano makes destructive eruptions. Benbow's last eruption (in 1913) caused the evacuation of the locals to Mele, close to Port Vila (Efate Island) . In March 2017, Google Streetview added the Marum crater with its lava lakes. Ambrym Island attracts tourists with its active volcanoes, tropical vegetation, local customs, and traditional accommodations (bungalows). The island can be accessed by sea (cruise ships and chartered tour boats) and also via two airports - Ulei (south-east coast) and Craig Cove (central-west coast). Both airports serve only domestic flights (by the flag carrier Air Vanuatu) linking to Luganville (Espiritu Santo) , Malakula Island (Norsup) and Paama Island. Vanuatu Islands (officially Republic of Vanuatu) is an island nation located in the South Pacific. The islands cover a total area of approx 12190 km2 (4706 mi2) and population around 290,000. Large cruise ships to Vanuatu Islands dock (anchor) either at Luganville or Champagne Bay (near Hog Harbour, in the northeast part of Espiritu Santo Island). The archipelago is of volcanic origin and is situated some 1750 km (1090 mi) east of northern Australia, east of New Guinea, 540 km (340 mi) northeast of New Caledonia, west of Fiji and southeast of Solomon Islands . The tourism industry in Vanuatu is a major revenue source as the archipelago is widely recognised as a premier vacation travel destination - especially for coral reef scuba diving. A unique attraction to scuba divers is the wreck of the US luxury cruise ship President Coolidge (converted troop carrier) on Espiritu Santo Island. Sunk during WW2 (1939-1945), the vessel is among the world's largest shipwrecks accessible for recreational diving. Independent sightseeing limited. Ambrym is a remote volcanic island with basic infrastructure, unsealed roads and no conventional cruise terminal. Most visitors experience the island through activities arranged by the ship or local community. Passengers should expect a tender landing rather than a pier. Access may involve stepping onto a beach, uneven ground or a basic landing area, so assistance may be needed for travelers with limited mobility. Sea conditions can delay, relocate or cancel tender operations. Follow the ship’s instructions because the landing village and available activities may change between calls.
terminal_notes: Ambrym is a remote volcanic island with basic infrastructure, unsealed roads and no conventional cruise terminal. Passengers should expect a tender landing rather than a pier.
tender_evidence: Passengers should expect a tender landing rather than a pier.

things_to_do.name: Join a Village Cultural Visit
things_to_do.description: This is normally the most practical Ambrym experience. Depending on arrangements made for the ship, a visit may include traditional dancing, sand drawing, carving, local stories and an introduction to village life. Ambrym’s ceremonies and Rom dances are part of living kastom rather than routine entertainment. Remain with the hosted group, follow local instructions and ask before photographing people, masks, performances or ceremonial places.

things_to_do.name: Explore Around the Landing Village
things_to_do.description: If passengers are permitted to move independently, a short walk near the landing may reveal village homes, gardens, coastal scenery and black volcanic sand. Paths can be rough, muddy or slippery, and there may be few signs or visitor facilities. Do not enter private land, ceremonial areas or inland tracks without permission. A local host is preferable even for a seemingly simple village walk.

things_to_do.name: Watch a Rom Dance or Cultural Demonstration
things_to_do.description: Some cruise calls include a specially arranged performance featuring masked dancers in elaborate costumes. Availability depends entirely on local arrangements and should not be assumed. These events are best attended through the ship’s program or an organized community visit.

things_to_do.name: Take an Organized Scenic Drive
things_to_do.description: Where vehicles are arranged, a local truck or four-wheel-drive trip may provide access to another village, forest scenery or volcanic landscapes. Roads are unsealed, journeys can be slow and rides may be rough. This option is unsuitable for passengers with significant back or mobility problems.

things_to_do.name: Volcano Trekking
things_to_do.description: Ambrym’s Benbow and Marum volcanic area is a major attraction, but reaching it involves local transport, an experienced guide and a long, strenuous trek over jungle trails, ash plains and exposed volcanic terrain. Many routes require a full day or an overnight expedition. A crater trek should only be considered when specifically organized for the cruise call with enough time, safety support and current authorization. The former persistent lava lakes disappeared after the 2018 eruption, so visitors should not expect to see a glowing lava lake.

Amelia Island FL (Fernandina Beach port locode USFEB ) is one of the USA's few unspoiled island paradises. It is located in the southernmost Atlantic coast (East Coast USA) barrier islands, stretching from North Carolina down to Florida. Fernandina Beach (population around 12,000) is Florida's northernmost city and part of Greater Jacksonville (metro). Island's rich history, lush, natural setting, uncrowded beaches, moss-covered oaks, unparalleled vacation experience (boating, fishing, golfing), stunning sunrises and sunsets, and the friendly "locals" make Amelia Island more than just a leisure travel destination. Fernandina Beach is the birthplace of the contemporary shrimping industry and most days shrimp boats depart from its docks. The 50-block historic district features classic Victorian-style architecture. Florida's oldest saloon is on Centre Street. Another must-see landmark is Fort Clinch (built before the Civil War). The island was first settled in 1735 by the British soldier James Edward Oglethorpe (1696-1785) and became part of East Florida (then Spanish territory) in 1783. In 1821 it was ceded to the USA with the rest of the state. The island has a total of 7 premium golf courses. The resort Omni at Amelia has 3 - Long Point, Oakmarsh and Ocean Links. Island's Golf Club is at the Summer Beach Resort. Amelia River Golf Club is nearby, as well as Fernandina Beach Golf Club. As cruise port destination, Amelia Island FL is included in the schedule of the USA's largest river cruise company - ACL-American Cruise Lines . The next tables show the company's 7-day itineraries as riverport sequences and prices per person (double occupancy). (ship American Star ) 7-day "Great Rivers of Florida" itinerary from homeport Jacksonville, from ~USD 2900 pp (ship American Independence ) 7-day itinerary between homeports Charleston and Jacksonville, from ~USD 3300 pp Cruise ships to Amelia Island dock (anchor) at Fernandina Beach - port town on the northwestern coast. Amelia Island calls normally place passengers at or near Fernandina Harbor Marina, immediately beside the historic center of Fernandina Beach. Small coastal ships may dock, while other calls may involve anchoring and a short tender transfer. Confirm the ship’s landing point and final tender time before going ashore. Independent sightseeing: Easy for downtown Fernandina Beach. The waterfront, Centre Street, historic buildings, shops and several museums are within comfortable walking distance. Fort Clinch, Atlantic beaches and other parts of the island require a taxi, cruise excursion or prearranged transport.
getting_from_port: Fernandina Harbor Marina: Centre Street begins beside the marina, so no shuttle is normally needed for downtown sightseeing. Alternative landing arrangements: The exact berth or tender point can vary. Follow the ship’s instructions rather than relying solely on the mapped port location. Taxis and rideshares: Useful for Fort Clinch, Main Beach and attractions beyond downtown. Availability may be limited when several activities finish together, so allow time for the return. Public transport: NassauTRANSIT serves the county, but its limited routes are less convenient than a taxi for a short cruise call. Trolley tours: Narrated tours commonly depart near the waterfront and cover downtown, Old Town and residential districts. Schedules vary and should be checked after arrival or reserved in advance.
tender_evidence: Small coastal ships may dock, while other calls may involve anchoring and a short tender transfer.

things_to_do.name: Historic Fernandina Beach
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–4 hours. This is the easiest independent option. Walk along Centre Street past Victorian commercial buildings, local shops and restaurants, then explore the quieter residential streets south of downtown. The Amelia Island Museum of History, housed in a former county jail, is about 0.6 km (0.4 mi) from the marina.

things_to_do.name: Fort Clinch State Park
things_to_do.description: Allow 2.5–4 hours, including transport. The preserved 19th-century fort overlooks Cumberland Sound and is surrounded by maritime forest, trails and shoreline. Use a taxi, rideshare or organized excursion. The park entrance is roughly 4 km (2.5 mi) from downtown, but the fort itself lies several additional miles inside the park, making the complete journey impractical on foot.

things_to_do.name: Amelia River Wildlife Cruise
things_to_do.description: Allow about 2–3 hours. Boat trips departing from Fernandina Harbor may explore the Amelia River, Cumberland Sound and waters near Cumberland Island, with possible views of dolphins, shorebirds, Fort Clinch and wild horses in the distance. This is practical independently when the departure and return times fit the ship’s call. Reserve ahead and confirm the boarding location.

things_to_do.name: Main Beach Park
things_to_do.description: Allow 2–3 hours. Main Beach is on the Atlantic side of the island, approximately 3.5 km (2.2 mi) from the marina. A taxi or rideshare is preferable to walking, especially in hot or humid weather. Facilities and nearby food options make it the most straightforward beach choice for a short visit.

things_to_do.name: Trolley or Island Highlights Tour
things_to_do.description: Allow 1.5–3 hours. A narrated trolley or cruise-organized tour is useful for passengers who want to see more than the compact downtown area without arranging several taxi journeys. Routes may include Old Town, Victorian neighborhoods and the island’s north end, but operating times are not guaranteed for every port call.

things_to_do.name: Egans Creek Greenway
things_to_do.description: The greenway offers grass-covered trails through wetlands where birds and other wildlife may be seen. things_to_do.name: Cumberland Island
things_to_do.description: Cumberland Island National Seashore lies across the state line in Georgia. Visiting it on foot usually requires a ferry from St. Marys, advance planning and substantial travel time, so it is generally unsuitable as an improvised cruise-day trip. A local sightseeing cruise that views its shoreline from the water is considerably more practical.

Amorgos Island (Katapola port locode GRKTP ) is the easternmost isle of Greece's Cyclades Islands group, as well as the nearest to the neighboring Dodecanese Islands group. Amorgos, along with its neighboring islets (the biggest of which is Nikouria) comprises the Amorgos municipality, with municipal land area approx 126 km2 (49 mi2), and population around 2,000. Due to the position of Amorgos Island opposite the ancient beaches of Ionian cities, such as Alikarnassos, Ephesos, and Militos, it became one of the first sites from which the Ionians passed through to Cyclades Islands and onto the Greek mainland. Throughout history, Amorgos Island was also popular as Yperia, Patagy (Platagy), Pagali, Psichia, and Karkisia. It features a wealth of remnants of old civilizations. At Archaic Greece's time, there were 3 independent city-states. They are believed to have had autonomous constitutions but a common currency. Amorgos Island is distinguished by the quality and size of the walls surrounding Arkesini city, by the ancient towers with remains scattered all over the isle, by the ancient tombs, stone tools, vases, inscriptions, and other antiquities. Panagia Hozoviotissa monastery is situated northeast of Chora, on the cliffside. It was built early in the 2nd millennium to protect a religious icon, which dates back to 812, from intruders. The unique icon is on public display in the monastery. Visitors must be dressed decently if they want to enter. As of July 2012, Panagia Hozoviotissa monastery is active and houses 3 practicing monks. Tourism on Amorgos Island is going up slowly, though its features prevent mass tourism. Amorgos is accessible only by boat. The three main places of tourist accommodations are Aegiali, Chora, and Katapola. Hiking ways are well-maintained. Other activities are related to wellness and also include scuba diving. Amorgos Island was featured in The Big Blue, a film by Luc Besson (1988). Agia Anna and Panagia Hozoviotissa monastery can be seen in it. Amorgos was also featured in Ariadni, a film by Giorgos Kordelas (2002). Amsterdam is The Netherlands' capital city and a major North Sea port (via IJmuiden ), as well as Amstel (Rhine) river cruise port. Port's cruise schedule includes mainly ships with roundtrip UK and Baltic Sea itineraries. Amsterdam is also a turnaround/homeport for riverboat cruises, serving itineraries on Rhine, Moselle and the Dutch inland waterways. The city has population around 1 million (urban 1,35 million, metro over 2,43 million). Randstad Megalopolis (which besides Amsterdam also includes Rotterdam and The Hague ) has population around 7 million. Amsterdam City itself is one of the world's most visited tourist travel destinations, and one of Europe's art capitals. It has a unique history, large canal ring, world-famous museums, a huge selection of guided city tours and shore excursions. On cruise shore excursions (roundtrip bus tours from Amsterdam) can be visited Almere (Southern Flevoland). IMPORTANT : On July 22, 2023, the city council voted to ban sea-going cruise vessels in order to restrict mass tourism and reduce air and noise pollution. The ban could result in the closure and relocation of the Port's main cruise terminal on IJ. In September 2023, the city introduced significantly increased taxes for visiting tourists, including via cruise ships. The new taxes are for hotel guests (12,5% over the room charge) and for cruise tourists (EUR 11 pp/~37% increase over the old charge to EUR 8 pp). In June 2024, Amsterdam City Council voted to limit the number of cruise ship calls starting in 2026. The strategy also includes plans for the relocation of the Passenger Terminal Amsterdam from downtown. Current municipal rules allow max 190 calls from ocean-going cruise vessels per year. Since July 2024, the Passenger Terminal Amsterdam is limited to a single berth daily. Starting January 2026, the terminal's annual limit will be 100 ship berthings. Additionally, by 2027, all docking ships will be required to use cold ironing/shore-side power . In August 2025, was announced an intention to limit annual river cruise ship visits to 1150 vessels. According to the city’s data, 1950 riverboat calls were recorded in 2024. Port Amsterdam (officially "Haven van Amsterdam", locode NLAMS) is a major seaport serving Amsterdam City. It is currently ranked Baltic Sea's 2nd largest cargo port (after Aarhus ). The port is on a former bay and via Noordzeekanaal is connected to the North Sea. The next photo shows the sea cruise port and its passenger terminal building. In the 17th-century (during the so-called Dutch Golden Age), Amsterdam was one of the main seaports of the Dutch East India Company - the world's first-ever multinational corporation (1602-established). Today, it is Netherlands' second-largest cargo port - after Rotterdam . Port's 2014 statistics showed as handled marine shipping cargo ~97,4 million tons. For comparison, in 2008 the port handled 6029 marine vessels with 75,8 million tons of cargo and 435,129 TEUs (containers). Annually, Port Amsterdam handles ~50,000 vessels (seagoing, riverboats, barges). Port's total area is 6,2 km2 (2,4 mi2) waterways and plus 20 km2 (7,7 mi2) land areas (quays, roads, railways, green areas). The port comprises several harbors, which are also part of city boroughs (named Westpoort, Westerpark, Centrum, Zeeburg). The list of harbours (haven) includes Afrika, Amerika, West Harbour, Jan van Riebeeck, Petroleum, Coen, Mercurius, Hout, De Ruijter Quay (Ruijterkade), Eastern Trade Quay. In 2017, Netherlands's positive economy led to a 2,5% increase in shipping volumes at Port Amsterdam - up to 81,3 million cargo tons. Together with other North Sea Canal ports, the total transshipment volume reached the record 100,8 million cargo tons. In Port IJmuiden the growth was 7% (up to 18,5 million tons). Port Beverwijk's increase was 6% (800,000 million tons). Port Zaanstad's increase was 35% (300,000 tons). Port's increase in Ro-Ro shipping was 11% (1,9 million tons). Imports rose by 4% (up to 50,9 million tons). Exports remained unchanged (30,4 million tons). In 2017 were allocated 18 hectares of land (11 hectares in 2016). Land recipients were Bio Energy Netherlands (biomass power station generating from waste timber electricity and raw materials for the country's chemical industry) and Chaincraft (biotech company converting biomass into fatty acids). Borghese Real Estate and DHL (logistics) expanded at Atlaspark. Two new facilities were realized at HoogTij park (Gam BAKKER, Container terminal CTV Vrede Steinweg) where Port Amsterdam is a participant. The port also acquired 10 hectares of land on the North Sea Canal's northern side. In November 2017, the port announced its objectives to achieve up to 50% emissions reduction (NOx, SOx, soot particles) generated by docked ocean cruise ships by the year 2030. Another planned objective was reducing to virtually zero the levels of noise and air pollution caused by diesel generators at all public berths (located inside the city's ring road) by 2018. In January 2018, Port Amsterdam signed with Titan LNG a long-term contract for the base (FlexFueler001, in America Harbour) of the company's bunkering pontoon. This was Europe's first such facility . Its central location in the harbour enables LNG transfers by both trucks and special vessels, making it independent from large-scale LNG terminals. America Harbour (draft 9,7 m) can handle both inland and ocean vessels alongside FlexFueler. The number of LNG-powered ships is rapidly growing (via drydock conversion and newbuilds ) as this fuel is cost-effective, suitable for various vessel types and environmentally friendly. LNG completely removes SOx and soot particles, reduces NOx emissions (up to 85%) as well as CO2 emissions. In August 2018, the port started offering a doubled "ESI discount" (Environmental Ship Index) for ESI-certified and LNG-powered vessels. In December 2018, Port Amsterdam conducted 4-week trials for MADS (Marine Anti Drone System). This program was for monitoring where and why drones (legal and illegal) fly over port's land areas. MADS detects and identifies flying drones within a 5 km (3 mi) range. The system provides GPS coordinates of both the device and its pilot, as well as the drone’s speed and course. More and more seaports worldwide begin to use drones for various purposes, including infrastructure inspections and environmental measurements. In mid-December 2018 started construction works on the Plastic Recycling Amsterdam project - a partnership with Umincorp (Rotterdam-based) and Milieu Service Nederland (Diemen-based). The new recycling plant has an annual capacity of 17,000 tons. The collected plastics are washed, shredded, separated (via Magnetic Density Separation), then sorted and processed into packaging materials. For FY2018 (fiscal year), Havenbedrijf Amsterdam NV (port authority) reported a net profit of EUR 68,5 million (12,5% increase over 2017's EUR 60,9 million) and revenue increase 5% (EUR 157,4 million), primarily due to land allocations totaling 45,1 hectares (18 hectares in 2017) and harbor fees increase due to increased transshipment cargo volume (82,3 million tons / 81,3 million in 2017). Port's added value increased 4% (to EUR 7,2 billion), the employment - by 2% (to 68,399 port-related jobs), North Sea Canal Area transshipment cargo volume reached 101,8 million tons. Port's total number of ship calls increased 7% (to 17,952 / 16,813 in 2017). The port handled 180 cruise ship calls plus 2007 riverboat cruise calls. Port’s investments amounted to EUR 53,3 million (40% increase over 2017's EUR 31,9 million). In March 2019, at Afrikahaven were inaugurated 4 new berths that serve inland liquid bulk carriers - blue cone-marked tankers shipping flammable materials. In the period November 2017 through February 2019, at Amsterdam's Afrikahaven port were constructed a total of 18 new berths (serving inland cargo ships with LOA lengths up to 135 m / 443 ft). The project also included adding 3 mooring quays (plus piles) and building a new concrete quay fitted with a drinking water supply station and a waste processing plant. For FY2019, Port Amsterdam reported a record transshipment volume of 86,3 million tonnes (6% increase over 2018's 82,3M tonnes). The transshipment growth was largely attributed to the 18% increase in energy products shipping (mainly coal and oil products), also dry bulk (+6%), TEU-containers (+12%), Ro-Ro shipping (+17%), chemical products (+3,4%), construction materials (+2,4%). Imports increased 5,7% (total 53,2M tonnes). Exports increased 5,5% (33,6M tonnes). In July 2022, HyCC Holding's subsidiary HyCC BV (Hydrogen Chemistry Company/2020-founded joint venture of Nobian and GIG-Green Investment Group) launched "Project H2era" (500-MW green hydrogen plant in the Port area) planned for completion in 2027. A similar but smaller (100-MW "Project H2ermes") was launched in Port IJmuiden. Both plants produce H2 and O2 from seawater via electrolysis (using renewable electricity). Cruise lines that include Amsterdam in their ship schedules increase every year. The terminal handles over 250,000 passengers during high season. One of Northern Europe's largest cruise ports, Amsterdam handles an average (ship calls) of 140+ ocean and 1500+ river cruises, The annual number of cruise tourists is around 700.000. In September 2015, MSC Splendida became port's largest cruise vessel. The seaport has 2 cruise terminals - Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (serving ocean ships) and another terminal located after the locks in IJmuiden. In 2017, the cruise port handled a total of 134 ship calls (125 in 2016) and 332,998 passengers (281,907 in 2016). At Port IJmuiden, cruise ship calls were 23 (32 in 2016). The total number of river cruise ship calls in 2017 was 1876. The number of river cruise passengers was 495,550.

Amsterdam Island (officially Amsterdamoya) is located off the northwest coast of Spitsbergen Island ( Svalbard Norway ). Amsterdamoya covers a total area of approx 17 km2 (7 mi2), of which around 12% is ice-covered. Amsterdam Island is separated from Danes Island via Danskegattet Strait. Isle's highest elevation point (Hiertabreen) is 472 m (1549 ft). The island was discovered in 1596 by Willem Barentsz (1550-1597). The Dutch occupied it in 1614, constructing a temporary whaling station on its southeastern promontory. A semi-permanent station (named Smeerenburg) was built here in 1619. During the 1640s, this settlement went into decline and eventually was abandoned by 1660. Currently, Amsterdamoya is uninhabited. Cruise ships to Amsterdam Island dock (anchor) at Smeerenburg - port station (uninhabited) on the southeastern coast.

Anacortes WA is a Pacific Northwest USA cruise port, cargo port (locode USOTS) and city on Fidalgo Island (Skagit County, Washington USA) with population around 16,000. The town's name consolidates the name "Anna Curtis" - the wife of Amos Bowman (early Fidalgo Island settlers). Anacortes is also one of two principal cities included in the Mount Vernon-Anacortes Metro Area. Anacortes is often visited via its Ferry Terminal that serves regular Washington State Ferries crossings interlinking with San Juan Islands (Lopez Island, Orcas Island, Shaw Island, San Juan Island) as well as with Victoria BC Canada (via Sidney BC) on Vancouver Island. A Skagit County-operated ferryboat serves Guemes Island (a residential island north of Anacortes, across Guemes Channel). Anacortes is surrounded by the North San Juan and Puget Sound Islands on three sides, as well as by Swinomish Channel and the Skagit Valley's flats to the east. The weather is milder than other Pacific Northwest regions, as it lies within the Olympic Mountain rain shadow. Anacortes WA is a popular destination for yachtsmen, leisure boaters and travelers to the San Juan Archipelago. It maintains a 0,89 km2 (220-acres) city park (on Fidalgo Island's northwestern end) named "Washington Park". The park features a marina/boat launching facility, camping sites, scenic views of San Juan Archipelago. The most beautiful view is of Cypress Island. As a result of the proximity to the Juan de Fuca Strait, the region also provides whale-watching opportunities. The waters off Fidalgo and Anacortes offer varieties of marine life, including 3 resident Orca pods. name: Anadyr (Russia)
summary: Anadyr is a port city in north-eastern Russia. It is located on the southern shore of Anadyr River's estuary, which empties into the Bering Sea. The city is Chukotka 's biggest, covering a total area of approx 20 km2 (8 mi2), with a population of around 15,000.
description: Anadyr is a port city in north-eastern Russia. It is located on the southern shore of Anadyr River's estuary, which empties into the Bering Sea. The city is Chukotka 's biggest, covering a total area of approx 20 km2 (8 mi2), with a population of around 15,000. Anadyr is a major port on the Northern Sea Route, located on the Gulf of Anadyr of Bering Sea and is linked to almost all important Russian Far Eastern seaports. Although the town has only been in existence for over a century, the origins of its name are much older. The name "Anadyr" initially derives from Yukaghir word "any-an", which means "river". The town of Anadyr lies at the tip of a big cape, to the north of which is situated the mouth of Anadyr River. To the east the estuarine part of the river, Anadyrsky Liman, emptying into the Gulf of Anadyr. The town itself is located on a gentle slope that rises up from the sea, and on the other side of Anadyr River are mountains. However, to the west, beyond the city are the vast expanses of flat tundra. Anadyr is very much a Soviet city with cement block apartment complexes lining the streets like barricades and the symbols of the Soviet era still found here and there. It has a meteorologic station and fishery factory. An interesting fact is that in 2011, the American theoretical physicist and cosmologist Paul Steinhardt (born December 25, 1952) led an international group of scientists who landed in Anadyr en route to an expedition into the Koryak Mountains in order to look for naturally occurring quasicrystals. To date, a total of three quasicrystals have been found from the material gathered on the expedition, including decagonite, icosahedrite, a yet unnamed 3rd natural quasicrystal, which is unlike anything previously synthesized in a laboratory. The team of Steinhbardt has established that natural quasicrystals were embedded in a meteorite that had hit the Earth around 15,000 years ago. Ancenis played a very important historical role as a key location on the road to Nantes , the historical capital of Brittany, which is 37 km (23 miles) to the southwest. It was named "the door of Brittany" and "the key of Brittany". Sights of interest in Ancenis include the medieval and Renaissance castle Château d'Ancenis, Loire river on which Ancenis is situated (on the north bank), Chapel of the Ursulines, Church of Saint Peter, Chapel Notre-Dame de Delivrance, Dolmen at Pierre-Couvretiere, Old quarter with medieval houses. Anchorage AK is Alaska's largest port city, located in Southern Alaska, between Turnagain and Knik arms of Cook Inlet and the Chugach Mountains. To the south is Kenai Peninsula, to the north is Denali National Park (aka Mount McKinley). Most cruise ship tourists visit Anchorage through Seward or Whittier . Anchorage AK serves as Alaska's hub for communications, transportation, and finance. The city has a population of around 300,000, ranking it Alaska's largest, containing over 40% of the state's total population. The city was founded in 1914 as the headquarters of the Alaska Railroad (Seward and Whittier) and via Anchorage to Fairbanks (north). With a population of around 32,000 (metro over 100,000), Fairbanks is ranked Alaska's 2nd most populous (after Anchorage). The local economy is based on tourism and air freight. In 1964 the city was devastated by an earthquake (aka Good Friday earthquake) and much of the downtown area had to be rebuilt. In 1968 was discovered the Prudhoe Bay Oil Field resulting in a boom in construction and oil companies setting up offices in the city. Anchorage is the cruise port to Fairbanks. The distance between both cities is around 580 km (360 mi). Travel time is 7-8 hours (by car and bus), 12 hours (by train) and 1 hour (by air). Train travel is the longest on Alaska Railroad. Being the most expensive, this is also the best way to enjoy the region's spectacular scenery as there are special glass-domed rail cars. From Anchorage are offered (as shore excursions) plane tours to Fairbanks. The most popular tourist attractions in Anchorage include Resolution Park, Museum of History and Art, Elderberry Park, Native Heritage Center, Earthquake Park, Eklutna Historical Park, Eagle River Nature Center, Portage Glacier. Also very popular are boat tours (via Seward ) to Prince William Sound's glaciers or Kenai Fjords Park. Bus and plane tours are offered to Denali National Park. Port Anchorage handles around 95% of all goods shipped to Alaska. Cargo ships from the US container shipping companies Horizon Lines and TOTE Maritime arrive twice per week from Port Tacoma (Washington). Along with handling cargoes, the port also serves as a jet fuel storage facility delivered from Alaskan refineries and used by the local US military base JBER (Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson) and TSAIA (Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport). Cruisetours starting in Anchorage AK often include bus travel to Talkeetna (Chugach Mountains), scenic train travel to Denali NP (Denali Education Center), an overnight stay in the Denali Park, return bus travel to Anchorage via Willow AK (popular for its dogsled- and ATV rides). The Wilderness Express Train links to Talkeetna AK, from where (via bus) is accessed Denali NP. Following the 2-year cruise shipping pause due to the COVID crisis, in 2022 Port Anchorage AK had scheduled only one ship call - by MS Nieuw Amsterdam (on Sept 15) as part of the 14-day "Great Alaskan Explorer" itinerary (roundtrip from Vancouver BC Canada ). Actually, many cruise ships to Anchorage actually dock in Whittier AK (visited on 7-day itineraries from Vancouver) and transport their passengers to Anchorage on bus excursions. Whittier is approx 100 km (60 mi) from Anchorage, accessible by road and train. At Port Anchorage, passengers can use bus shuttle service (usually complimentary), taxis and rental cars downtown. Shore excursions (by train and bus) also leave from the cruise terminal. Following the Coronavirus crisis, in 2022 Port Anchorage was visited by just one cruise ship - Holland America Line 's ms Nieuw Amsterdam .

Ancona is a port city on the Adriatic Sea and in Italy's Marche region, with a population of around 100,000. The cruise port is located at short walking distance to downtown, lined up with street markets and shops. Ancona is approx 280 km (170 mi) northeast of Civitavecchia-Rome and one of Italy's main ferry ports on the Adriatic. Fincantieri (one of the world's largest shipbuilding companies ) owns the merchant shipbuilding yards Monfalcone , Marghera ( Venice ), Sestri Ponente ( Genoa ), Ancona, Castellammare di Stabia (near Naples ) and Palermo (Sicily) . The company also owns the naval shipyards Riva Trigoso (Genoa) and Muggiano ( La Spezia ). On November 3, 2023, Fincantieri signed with ADSP (Central Adriatic Sea System Authority) an EUR 80 million deal for Ancona Port's development. The agreement was signed by Pierroberto Folgiero (Fincantieri’s CEO and Managing Director) and Vincenzo Garofalo (ADSP's President). By this project, the Port's existing infrastructure will be enhanced/expanded and upgraded by adding new construction piers, the existing drydock's expansion, and upgrades to all lifting facilities. The assets' development will result in increased capacity for handling larger ships (with bigger GT and DWT) from both the cruise and merchant sectors. Of the total EUR 80M investment, EUR 40M is public funding - EUR 20M for a new construction pier plus EUR 20M for the drydock's extension and securing the breakwater. The remaining EUR 40M are private investments (by Fincantieri SpA) as part of the new 40-year state concession of the Port. Fincantieri's investment is for advancing Ancona Port's shipbuilding activities. Regularly-scheduled cruiseferries link Ancona with Croatia ( Split , Zadar , Hvar Island ), Albania ( Durres ), Greece ( Patras , Igoumenitsa , Corfu ), Italy ( Venice ). Among the largest ferry companies are SNAV, Adria Ferries, Minoan Lines, Anek Superfast, Jadrolinija (Croatia). The town was founded by colonists from Syracuse in late-4th-century BC. In the 2nd-century BC, it was conquered by the Romans and developed a major port serving the Adriatic shipping trade. In the period 1532-1860, the city was directly ruled by the Roman Pope. City's best-known landmarks (most restored after the severe bombings during WW2 / 1939-45) include the Arch of Trajan (Roman Triumphal arch), Santa Maria Della Piazza Church (11th-century), San Ciriaco Cathedral (former Roman temple of Venus and a 5th-century basilica), Gothic-style buildings, Marche Museum, Piazza del Plebiscito. Port Ancona welcomed its largest-ever (homeported) cruise liner ( MSC Sinfonia ) in June 2016. MSC Cruises announced Sinfonia's 2016 Ancona deployment in the summer of 2015. Since then, the Port Authority developed all technical solutions for docking the vessel (length 276 m / 906 ft) at the port's wharf (length 200 m / 656 ft). Ancona was chosen by MSC due to its strategic position for regular calls on Adriatic Sea cruise ports.
